functions.name: crypto_aead_xchacha20poly1305_ietf_encrypt
functions.signature:

ad may be NULL only if adlen == 0; otherwise must point to at least adlen bytes of readable memory.
nsec must be NULL (crypto_aead_xchacha20poly1305_ietf_NSECBYTES == 0).
npub must point to crypto_aead_xchacha20poly1305_ietf_NPUBBYTES (24) bytes.
k must point to crypto_aead_xchacha20poly1305_ietf_KEYBYTES (32) bytes.
mlen must be <= crypto_aead_xchacha20poly1305_ietf_messagebytes_max().
The same (k, npub) pair must never be reused across encryptions (nonce uniqueness is required).
Pointers marked nonnull by attributes (c, npub, k) must not be NULL.
Return value 0 indicates success; negative values indicate failure.

functions.name: crypto_aead_xchacha20poly1305_ietf_decrypt
functions.signature:

On success, writes the plaintext into m and sets *mlen_p to the plaintext length if provided. Returns -1 on authentication failure; callers must check the return value (warn_unused_result). nsec is unused for this construction.

Pointers marked nonnull by attributes (c, npub, k) must not be NULL.

functions.name: crypto_auth_bytes

requirements: None beyond being callable at any time after the library is available.

functions.name: crypto_auth
functions.signature: SODIUM_EXPORT int crypto_auth(unsigned char *out, const unsigned char *in, unsigned long long inlen, const unsigned char *k) __attribute__ ((nonnull(1, 4)));
functions.description: Computes a message authentication code (MAC) of the input message using the secret key and writes it to out. Intended usage: allocate an out buffer of crypto_auth_BYTES bytes, pass the message and a crypto_auth_KEYBYTES-byte key.
requirements: out must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to a writable buffer of at least crypto_auth_BYTES bytes.
in may be NULL only if inlen is 0; otherwise it must point to at least inlen bytes of readable memory.

inlen is the length of the message in bytes and fits in unsigned long long.
On success, returns 0; callers should handle nonzero return codes as errors (exact error conditions not specified in this header).
The function may be called multiple times independently; no global initialization requirements are stated here.

functions.name: crypto_auth_verify
functions.signature: SODIUM_EXPORT int crypto_auth_verify(const unsigned char *h, const unsigned char *in, unsigned long long inlen, const unsigned char *k) __attribute__ ((warn_unused_result)) __attribute__ ((nonnull(1, 4)));
functions.description: Verifies that the authentication tag h is a valid MAC for the message in under the secret key k. Intended usage: provide a crypto_auth_BYTES-byte tag, the message, and a crypto_auth_KEYBYTES-byte key; check the return value.
requirements: h must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to a buffer containing a MAC of length crypto_auth_BYTES bytes.
in may be NULL only if inlen is 0; otherwise it must point to at least inlen bytes of readable memory.
k must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to a buffer of exactly crypto_auth_KEYBYTES bytes.
inlen is the length of the message in bytes and fits in unsigned long long.
Return value must be checked (warn_unused_result): returns 0 on successful verification and nonzero on failure (exact codes not specified here).

functions.name: crypto_auth_keygen
functions.description: Generates a new random secret key suitable for crypto_auth and stores it in k. Intended usage: allocate a buffer of crypto_auth_KEYBYTES bytes and pass it to receive the key.
requirements: k must be a non-NULL pointer to a writable buffer of at least crypto_auth_KEYBYTES bytes.
The buffer provided will be filled with key material; treat it as secret and handle securely (e.g., do not reuse as other key types).
No return value; caller must assume k is populated on success (no error reporting is defined in this header).

functions.name: crypto_auth_hmacsha256_bytes
functions.description: Returns the size in bytes of an HMAC-SHA-256 authentication tag produced by this API (constant: 32 bytes). Use this to allocate output buffers for tags.
requirements: No arguments; always safe to call.
Use the returned value to size the authentication tag buffer for related functions.

functions.name: crypto_auth_hmacsha256_keybytes
functions.description: Returns the size in bytes of a recommended/standard key for HMAC-SHA-256 in this API (constant: 32 bytes). Use this to allocate and validate key buffers.
requirements: No arguments; always safe to call.
Use the returned value to size the key buffer for crypto_auth_hmacsha256 and crypto_auth_hmacsha256_keygen.

functions.name: crypto_auth_hmacsha256
functions.description: Computes an HMAC-SHA-256 authentication tag over the input message and writes it to out. One-shot (non-streaming) convenience wrapper around the HMAC construction.
requirements: out must be a valid, writable buffer of at least crypto_auth_hmacsha256_bytes() bytes; it must not be NULL (nonnull parameter 1).
k (the key) must point to a readable buffer of length crypto_auth_hmacsha256_keybytes(); it must not be NULL (nonnull parameter 4).
in may be NULL only if inlen == 0; otherwise it must point to a readable buffer of at least inlen bytes.

Returns 0 on success; callers should handle nonzero return as an error.

functions.name: crypto_auth_hmacsha256_verify
functions.description: Verifies that the provided HMAC-SHA-256 tag h authenticates the message in under key k. Constant-time comparison on valid inputs is expected by convention for this API.
requirements: h must point to a readable buffer containing exactly crypto_auth_hmacsha256_bytes() bytes; it must not be NULL (nonnull parameter 1).
k (the key) must point to a readable buffer of length crypto_auth_hmacsha256_keybytes(); it must not be NULL (nonnull parameter 4).
in may be NULL only if inlen == 0; otherwise it must point to a readable buffer of at least inlen bytes.
inlen is the length of the input message in bytes.
Return value must be checked (warn_unused_result): returns 0 if verification succeeds, and a nonzero value (typically -1) if verification fails.

functions.name: crypto_auth_hmacsha256_statebytes
functions.description: Returns the size in bytes of the crypto_auth_hmacsha256_state structure used by the streaming HMAC-SHA-256 API. Useful for dynamic allocation or ABI checks.
requirements: No arguments; always safe to call.

functions.name: crypto_auth_hmacsha256_init
functions.description: Initializes an HMAC-SHA-256 streaming state with the provided key, preparing it for zero or more update calls followed by a final call to produce the tag.
requirements: state must be a valid, writable pointer to storage at least crypto_auth_hmacsha256_statebytes() bytes in size; it must not be NULL (nonnull).

Must be called before crypto_auth_hmacsha256_update and crypto_auth_hmacsha256_final on the same state.

functions.name: crypto_auth_hmacsha256_update

requirements: state must be a valid pointer to a state previously initialized with crypto_auth_hmacsha256_init; it must not be NULL (nonnull parameter 1).

Returns 0 on success; callers should handle nonzero return as an error.
Do not use a state concurrently from multiple threads without external synchronization.

functions.name: crypto_auth_hmacsha256_final
functions.description: Finalizes the HMAC-SHA-256 computation for the given streaming state and writes the authentication tag to out. The state is consumed for this computation.
requirements: state must be a valid pointer to a state previously initialized with crypto_auth_hmacsha256_init and updated zero or more times; it must not be NULL (nonnull).
out must be a valid, writable buffer of at least crypto_auth_hmacsha256_bytes() bytes; it must not be NULL (nonnull).
Returns 0 on success; callers should handle nonzero return as an error.
After final, the state should not be reused unless reinitialized.

functions.name: crypto_auth_hmacsha256_keygen
functions.description: Generates a fresh, uniformly random key suitable for HMAC-SHA-256 and writes it to the provided buffer. Convenience utility to obtain a key of size crypto_auth_hmacsha256_KEYBYTES.

functions.name: crypto_auth_hmacsha512_bytes

functions.name: crypto_auth_hmacsha512_keybytes
functions.description: Returns the required key size in bytes for the HMAC-SHA-512 one-shot interface and key generator. Use this to size key buffers for crypto_auth_hmacsha512() and crypto_auth_hmacsha512_keygen().
requirements: No arguments; safe to call at any time.
Use the returned value to allocate or validate key buffers (must be crypto_auth_hmacsha512_KEYBYTES bytes for one-shot and keygen).

functions.signature: int crypto_auth_hmacsha512(unsigned char *out, const unsigned char *in, unsigned long long inlen, const unsigned char *k) __attribute__ ((nonnull(1, 4)));
functions.description: Computes a HMAC-SHA-512 authenticator (tag) over the input message using the provided secret key. Writes a crypto_auth_hmacsha512_BYTES-byte tag to out and returns 0 on success. Intended for one-shot authentication of a contiguous message buffer.
requirements: out must be a non-NULL pointer to a buffer of at least crypto_auth_hmacsha512_BYTES bytes.

functions.name: crypto_auth_hmacsha512_verify
functions.signature: int crypto_auth_hmacsha512_verify(const unsigned char *h, const unsigned char *in, unsigned long long inlen, const unsigned char *k) __attribute__ ((warn_unused_result)) __attribute__ ((nonnull(1, 4)));
functions.description: Verifies that the provided HMAC-SHA-512 tag h matches the tag computed over the message in with key k. Returns 0 if the tag is valid, and -1 (nonzero) if verification fails. Designed for constant-time comparison to avoid timing leaks; callers must use the return value.
requirements: h must be a non-NULL pointer to a buffer containing exactly crypto_auth_hmacsha512_BYTES bytes.
k must be a non-NULL pointer to a buffer of at least crypto_auth_hmacsha512_KEYBYTES bytes.
in may be NULL only if inlen is 0; otherwise it must point to inlen bytes of readable memory.
The return value is annotated warn_unused_result; callers must check it and handle verification failure (nonzero).

functions.name: crypto_auth_hmacsha512_statebytes
functions.description: Returns the size in bytes of the incremental HMAC-SHA-512 state structure. Useful for allocating state dynamically or validating structure size assumptions.
requirements: No arguments; safe to call at any time.

functions.name: crypto_auth_hmacsha512_init
functions.signature: int crypto_auth_hmacsha512_init(crypto_auth_hmacsha512_state *state, const unsigned char *key, size_t keylen) __attribute__ ((nonnull));
functions.description: Initializes an incremental HMAC-SHA-512 computation with the provided key, writing initialization data into state. After init, call crypto_auth_hmacsha512_update() zero or more times, then crypto_auth_hmacsha512_final() to obtain the tag.
requirements: state must be a non-NULL pointer to a writable crypto_auth_hmacsha512_state object of at least crypto_auth_hmacsha512_statebytes() bytes.
key must be a non-NULL pointer to keylen bytes of readable memory; keylen may be any size representable by size_t (the HMAC construction handles arbitrary key lengths).
Must be called before the first update/final for a given state.
Return value should be checked by the caller (0 indicates success; nonzero indicates failure).

functions.name: crypto_auth_hmacsha512_update
functions.signature: int crypto_auth_hmacsha512_update(crypto_auth_hmacsha512_state *state, const unsigned char *in, unsigned long long inlen) __attribute__ ((nonnull(1)));
functions.description: Feeds additional message data into an in-progress incremental HMAC-SHA-512 computation initialized with crypto_auth_hmacsha512_init(). Can be called multiple times to process a message in chunks.
requirements: state must be a non-NULL pointer to an initialized crypto_auth_hmacsha512_state (initialized via crypto_auth_hmacsha512_init).
in may be NULL only if inlen is 0; otherwise it must point to inlen bytes of readable memory.
May be called zero or more times between init and final; do not call after final unless reinitialized with init.
Return value should be checked by the caller (0 indicates success; nonzero indicates failure).

functions.name: crypto_auth_hmacsha512_final
functions.description: Finalizes an incremental HMAC-SHA-512 computation and writes the crypto_auth_hmacsha512_BYTES-byte tag to out. The state is consumed by final; reinitialize to compute a new tag.
requirements: state must be a non-NULL pointer to a crypto_auth_hmacsha512_state previously initialized with crypto_auth_hmacsha512_init and updated zero or more times.
out must be a non-NULL pointer to a buffer of at least crypto_auth_hmacsha512_BYTES bytes.
After calling final, the state must not be used again unless reinitialized with init.
Return value should be checked by the caller (0 indicates success; nonzero indicates failure).

functions.name: crypto_auth_hmacsha512_keygen
functions.description: Generates a new random key suitable for use with HMAC-SHA-512 one-shot and incremental APIs, writing crypto_auth_hmacsha512_KEYBYTES bytes to k.
requirements: k must be a non-NULL pointer to a writable buffer of at least crypto_auth_hmacsha512_KEYBYTES bytes.
Caller is responsible for securely storing and handling the generated key.
Must not be called with overlapping or read-only memory for k.

functions.name: crypto_auth_hmacsha512256_bytes
functions.description: Returns the length in bytes of an HMAC-SHA-512/256 authentication tag (MAC). Expected usage: call to size buffers for MAC outputs; value equals crypto_auth_hmacsha512256_BYTES (32).
requirements: None beyond standard calling conventions; function takes no arguments and returns a constant size.

functions.name: crypto_auth_hmacsha512256_keybytes
functions.description: Returns the required key size in bytes for HMAC-SHA-512/256 one-shot/auth APIs. Expected usage: call to size or validate keys; value equals crypto_auth_hmacsha512256_KEYBYTES (32).
requirements: None beyond standard calling conventions; function takes no arguments and returns a constant size.

functions.name: crypto_auth_hmacsha512256
functions.description: Computes an HMAC-SHA-512/256 authentication tag (32 bytes) over the input message using the provided secret key. Expected usage: allocate a 32-byte output buffer, pass the message pointer/length and a 32-byte key; on success, out receives the MAC and the function returns 0 (libsodium convention).
requirements: out must be non-NULL and point to a writable buffer of at least crypto_auth_hmacsha512256_BYTES (32) bytes (nonnull(1)).
k must be non-NULL and point to a readable buffer of exactly crypto_auth_hmacsha512256_KEYBYTES (32) bytes (nonnull(4)).
If inlen > 0, in must point to a readable buffer with at least inlen bytes; if inlen == 0, in may be NULL or a valid pointer.
Caller should check the return value; 0 indicates success, non-zero indicates failure per libsodium conventions.
The same key must be used for both authentication and verification of a given message/stream.

functions.name: crypto_auth_hmacsha512256_verify
functions.description: Verifies that the provided HMAC-SHA-512/256 tag h authenticates the message in using the secret key k. Expected usage: pass a 32-byte tag, the message pointer/length, and the 32-byte key; returns 0 if the tag is valid, -1 otherwise (libsodium convention). warn_unused_result indicates callers must check the return value.
requirements: h must be non-NULL and point to a readable buffer of exactly crypto_auth_hmacsha512256_BYTES (32) bytes (nonnull(1)).
k must be non-NULL and point to a readable buffer of exactly crypto_auth_hmacsha512256_KEYBYTES (32) bytes (nonnull(4)).
If inlen > 0, in must point to a readable buffer with at least inlen bytes; if inlen == 0, in may be NULL or a valid pointer.
Caller must check and handle the return value (warn_unused_result): 0 means verification succeeded; non-zero indicates failure; treat any non-zero as authentication failure.
Do not reuse unrelated keys; use the same key that was used to compute the tag being verified.

functions.name: crypto_auth_hmacsha512256_statebytes
functions.description: Returns the size in bytes of the incremental HMAC-SHA-512/256 state object (crypto_auth_hmacsha512256_state). Expected usage: allocate state buffers dynamically or validate sizing for incremental API.
requirements: None beyond standard calling conventions; function takes no arguments and returns the size needed for a state object.

functions.name: crypto_auth_hmacsha512256_init
functions.description: Initializes an incremental HMAC-SHA-512/256 state with the provided key. After init, call update zero or more times, then final to produce the 32-byte tag. Returns 0 on success (libsodium convention). Key length may be arbitrary as per HMAC; using crypto_auth_hmacsha512256_KEYBYTES (32) is recommended.
requirements: state must be non-NULL and point to writable memory of at least crypto_auth_hmacsha512256_statebytes() bytes (nonnull).
key must be non-NULL and point to a readable buffer of at least keylen bytes (nonnull).
keylen is the key length in bytes; the buffer at key must contain at least keylen accessible bytes; zero-length keys are allowed by HMAC semantics.
Caller should check the return value; 0 indicates success, non-zero indicates failure per libsodium conventions.
state must not be used before successful initialization; reinitialize before reusing after a prior final.

functions.name: crypto_auth_hmacsha512256_update
functions.description: Feeds message data into an initialized incremental HMAC-SHA-512/256 state. May be called multiple times to process a message in chunks. Returns 0 on success (libsodium convention).
requirements: state must be non-NULL, writable, and previously initialized via crypto_auth_hmacsha512256_init (nonnull(1)).
If inlen > 0, in must point to a readable buffer with at least inlen bytes; if inlen == 0, in may be NULL or a valid pointer.
Caller should check the return value; 0 indicates success, non-zero indicates failure per libsodium conventions.
Do not call update after a final on the same state unless it has been reinitialized.

functions.name: crypto_auth_hmacsha512256_final
functions.description: Finalizes the incremental HMAC-SHA-512/256 computation and writes the 32-byte authentication tag to out. Returns 0 on success (libsodium convention). After final, the state should be considered consumed until reinitialized.
requirements: state must be non-NULL and must have been initialized with crypto_auth_hmacsha512256_init and updated as needed (nonnull).
out must be non-NULL and point to a writable buffer of at least crypto_auth_hmacsha512256_BYTES (32) bytes (nonnull).
Caller should check the return value; 0 indicates success, non-zero indicates failure per libsodium conventions.
Do not reuse the state for further updates after final unless reinitialized.

functions.name: crypto_auth_hmacsha512256_keygen
functions.description: Generates a fresh random key suitable for HMAC-SHA-512/256 (32 bytes) and writes it to k. Expected usage: allocate a 32-byte buffer and call to obtain a key for crypto_auth_hmacsha512256 or verify.
requirements: k must be non-NULL and point to a writable buffer of at least crypto_auth_hmacsha512256_KEYBYTES (32) bytes (nonnull).
The generated key is secret; callers must handle and store it securely and avoid reuse across unrelated protocols or purposes.

functions.name: crypto_box_seedbytes
functions.description: Returns the number of bytes required for a seed used with crypto_box_seed_keypair(). Use this to size the seed buffer.
requirements: No arguments.
Return value is the exact seed length required for crypto_box_seed_keypair().

functions.name: crypto_box_publickeybytes
functions.description: Returns the size in bytes of a crypto_box public key. Use this to allocate pk buffers and to validate inputs.
requirements: No arguments.
Return value is the exact size required for public keys passed to crypto_box* APIs.

functions.name: crypto_box_secretkeybytes
functions.description: Returns the size in bytes of a crypto_box secret (private) key. Use this to allocate sk buffers and to validate inputs.
requirements: No arguments.
Return value is the exact size required for secret keys passed to crypto_box* APIs.

functions.name: crypto_box_noncebytes
functions.description: Returns the size in bytes of the nonce required by crypto_box* operations. Use this to size/validate nonces.
requirements: No arguments.
Return value is the exact nonce size required by functions taking a nonce parameter.

functions.name: crypto_box_macbytes
functions.description: Returns the size in bytes of the authentication tag (MAC) produced/verified by crypto_box* functions.
requirements: No arguments.
For easy variants, ciphertext length = message length + crypto_box_macbytes().
For detached variants, MAC buffer must be exactly crypto_box_macbytes() bytes.

functions.name: crypto_box_messagebytes_max
functions.description: Returns the maximum message length (in bytes) that crypto_box* can process on this platform/implementation.
requirements: No arguments.
Callers should ensure message lengths do not exceed this value.

functions.name: crypto_box_primitive
functions.description: Returns the name of the underlying primitive used by this crypto_box implementation ("curve25519xsalsa20poly1305").
requirements: No arguments.
Returned pointer refers to a static, null-terminated string; do not free.

functions.name: crypto_box_seed_keypair
functions.signature: int crypto_box_seed_keypair(unsigned char *pk, unsigned char *sk, const unsigned char *seed);
functions.description: Derives a deterministic public/secret keypair from a seed. Use when you need reproducible keypairs.
requirements: pk must point to a buffer of size crypto_box_publickeybytes().
sk must point to a buffer of size crypto_box_secretkeybytes().
seed must point to a buffer of size crypto_box_seedbytes().
All three pointers must be non-NULL (nonnull attribute).
Return value must be checked (warn_unused_result). 0 indicates success; non-zero indicates failure.
Thread-safety is not specially constrained beyond general note; no specific sodium_init() requirement stated here.

functions.name: crypto_box_keypair
functions.description: Generates a random crypto_box public/secret keypair.
requirements: pk must point to a buffer of size crypto_box_publickeybytes().
sk must point to a buffer of size crypto_box_secretkeybytes().
pk and sk must be non-NULL (nonnull attribute).
Return value must be checked (warn_unused_result implied by common practice; attribute not present here, but callers should still check).
For thread safety, sodium_init() should be called before using this function (per header comment).

functions.name: crypto_box_easy
functions.signature: int crypto_box_easy(unsigned char *c, const unsigned char *m, unsigned long long mlen, const unsigned char *n, const unsigned char *pk, const unsigned char *sk);
functions.description: Encrypts and authenticates a message m using the recipient's public key and the sender's secret key, writing the ciphertext (including MAC) to c.
requirements: c must point to a buffer of size mlen + crypto_box_macbytes().
m must point to a buffer of size mlen (may be zero-length if m != NULL).
n (nonce) must be non-NULL and exactly crypto_box_noncebytes() bytes.
pk must be non-NULL and exactly crypto_box_publickeybytes() bytes.
sk must be non-NULL and exactly crypto_box_secretkeybytes() bytes.
Pointers c, n, pk, sk must be non-NULL (nonnull(1,4,5,6)).
Return value must be checked (warn_unused_result). 0 indicates success; -1 indicates failure (e.g., misuse).
mlen should not exceed crypto_box_messagebytes_max().

functions.name: crypto_box_open_easy
functions.signature: int crypto_box_open_easy(unsigned char *m, const unsigned char *c, unsigned long long clen, const unsigned char *n, const unsigned char *pk, const unsigned char *sk);
functions.description: Verifies and decrypts a ciphertext c produced by crypto_box_easy(), writing the plaintext to m.
requirements: c must be non-NULL and of length clen, where clen >= crypto_box_macbytes().
m must point to a buffer of size clen - crypto_box_macbytes().
n must be non-NULL and exactly crypto_box_noncebytes() bytes.
pk must be non-NULL and exactly crypto_box_publickeybytes() bytes.
sk must be non-NULL and exactly crypto_box_secretkeybytes() bytes.
Pointers c, n, pk, sk must be non-NULL (nonnull(2,4,5,6)).
Return value must be checked (warn_unused_result). On authentication failure, returns -1 and m must be considered uninitialized/invalid.
Plaintext length (clen - MAC) should not exceed crypto_box_messagebytes_max().

functions.name: crypto_box_detached
functions.signature: int crypto_box_detached(unsigned char *c, unsigned char *mac, const unsigned char *m, unsigned long long mlen, const unsigned char *n, const unsigned char *pk, const unsigned char *sk);
functions.description: Encrypts a message m and writes the ciphertext to c and the authentication tag to mac (detached mode).
requirements: c must point to a buffer of size mlen.
mac must point to a buffer of size crypto_box_macbytes().
m must point to a buffer of size mlen (may be zero-length if m != NULL).
n must be non-NULL and exactly crypto_box_noncebytes() bytes.
pk must be non-NULL and exactly crypto_box_publickeybytes() bytes.
sk must be non-NULL and exactly crypto_box_secretkeybytes() bytes.
c, mac, n, pk, sk must be non-NULL (nonnull(1,2,5,6,7)).
Return value must be checked (warn_unused_result). 0 indicates success; non-zero indicates failure.
mlen should not exceed crypto_box_messagebytes_max().

functions.name: crypto_box_open_detached
functions.signature: int crypto_box_open_detached(unsigned char *m, const unsigned char *c, const unsigned char *mac, unsigned long long clen, const unsigned char *n, const unsigned char *pk, const unsigned char *sk);
functions.description: Verifies the detached MAC and decrypts the ciphertext c into m.
requirements: m must point to a buffer of size clen.
c must be non-NULL and of length clen.
mac must be non-NULL and exactly crypto_box_macbytes() bytes.
n must be non-NULL and exactly crypto_box_noncebytes() bytes.
pk must be non-NULL and exactly crypto_box_publickeybytes() bytes.
sk must be non-NULL and exactly crypto_box_secretkeybytes() bytes.
c, mac, n, pk, sk must be non-NULL (nonnull(2,3,5,6,7)).
Return value must be checked (warn_unused_result). On authentication failure, returns -1 and m must be considered uninitialized/invalid.
clen should not exceed crypto_box_messagebytes_max().

functions.name: crypto_box_beforenmbytes
functions.description: Returns the size in bytes of a shared key produced by crypto_box_beforenm().
requirements: No arguments.
Returned size is required to allocate the k buffer for *_afternm functions.

functions.name: crypto_box_beforenm
functions.signature: int crypto_box_beforenm(unsigned char *k, const unsigned char *pk, const unsigned char *sk);
functions.description: Computes a shared key k from a peer's public key and a local secret key for use with the *_afternm APIs.
requirements: k must point to a buffer of size crypto_box_beforenmbytes().
pk must be non-NULL and exactly crypto_box_publickeybytes() bytes.
sk must be non-NULL and exactly crypto_box_secretkeybytes() bytes.
All pointers must be non-NULL (nonnull).
Return value must be checked (warn_unused_result). 0 indicates success; non-zero indicates failure.

functions.name: crypto_box_easy_afternm
functions.signature: int crypto_box_easy_afternm(unsigned char *c, const unsigned char *m, unsigned long long mlen, const unsigned char *n, const unsigned char *k);
functions.description: Encrypts and authenticates a message using a precomputed shared key k (from crypto_box_beforenm()).
requirements: c must point to a buffer of size mlen + crypto_box_macbytes().
m must point to a buffer of size mlen (may be zero-length if m != NULL).
n must be non-NULL and exactly crypto_box_noncebytes() bytes.
k must be non-NULL and exactly crypto_box_beforenmbytes() bytes.
Pointers c, n, k must be non-NULL (nonnull(1,4,5)).
Return value should be checked (no warn_unused_result attribute here, but failures must be handled).
mlen should not exceed crypto_box_messagebytes_max().

functions.name: crypto_box_open_easy_afternm
functions.signature: int crypto_box_open_easy_afternm(unsigned char *m, const unsigned char *c, unsigned long long clen, const unsigned char *n, const unsigned char *k);
functions.description: Verifies and decrypts a ciphertext produced by crypto_box_easy_afternm() (or easy + matching keys) using a precomputed shared key k.
requirements: m must point to a buffer of size clen - crypto_box_macbytes().
c must be non-NULL and of length clen, where clen >= crypto_box_macbytes().
n must be non-NULL and exactly crypto_box_noncebytes() bytes.
k must be non-NULL and exactly crypto_box_beforenmbytes() bytes.
c, n, k must be non-NULL (nonnull(2,4,5)).
Return value must be checked (warn_unused_result). On authentication failure, returns -1 and m must be considered uninitialized/invalid.
Plaintext length (clen - MAC) should not exceed crypto_box_messagebytes_max().

functions.name: crypto_box_detached_afternm
functions.signature: int crypto_box_detached_afternm(unsigned char *c, unsigned char *mac, const unsigned char *m, unsigned long long mlen, const unsigned char *n, const unsigned char *k);
functions.description: Encrypts a message using a precomputed shared key k and writes ciphertext to c and MAC to mac (detached mode).
requirements: c must point to a buffer of size mlen.
mac must point to a buffer of size crypto_box_macbytes().
m must point to a buffer of size mlen (may be zero-length if m != NULL).
n must be non-NULL and exactly crypto_box_noncebytes() bytes.
k must be non-NULL and exactly crypto_box_beforenmbytes() bytes.
c, mac, n, k must be non-NULL (nonnull(1,2,5,6)).
Return value should be checked.
mlen should not exceed crypto_box_messagebytes_max().

functions.name: crypto_box_open_detached_afternm
functions.signature: int crypto_box_open_detached_afternm(unsigned char *m, const unsigned char *c, const unsigned char *mac, unsigned long long clen, const unsigned char *n, const unsigned char *k);
functions.description: Verifies a detached MAC and decrypts ciphertext using a precomputed shared key k.
requirements: m must point to a buffer of size clen.
c must be non-NULL and of length clen.
mac must be non-NULL and exactly crypto_box_macbytes() bytes.
n must be non-NULL and exactly crypto_box_noncebytes() bytes.
k must be non-NULL and exactly crypto_box_beforenmbytes() bytes.
c, mac, n, k must be non-NULL (nonnull(2,3,5,6)).
Return value must be checked (warn_unused_result). On authentication failure, returns -1 and m must be considered uninitialized/invalid.
clen should not exceed crypto_box_messagebytes_max().

functions.name: crypto_box_sealbytes
functions.description: Returns the number of overhead bytes added by crypto_box_seal() to a message (SEALBYTES).
requirements: No arguments.
For sealing, ciphertext length = message length + crypto_box_sealbytes().

functions.name: crypto_box_seal
functions.signature: int crypto_box_seal(unsigned char *c, const unsigned char *m, unsigned long long mlen, const unsigned char *pk);
functions.description: Encrypts a message to a recipient using an ephemeral keypair; only the recipient's public key is required. The ciphertext includes the ephemeral public key and MAC.
requirements: c must point to a buffer of size mlen + crypto_box_sealbytes().
m must point to a buffer of size mlen (may be zero-length if m != NULL).
pk must be non-NULL and exactly crypto_box_publickeybytes() bytes.
c and pk must be non-NULL (nonnull(1,4)).
Return value should be checked; 0 indicates success, non-zero indicates failure.
mlen should not exceed crypto_box_messagebytes_max().

functions.name: crypto_box_seal_open
functions.signature: int crypto_box_seal_open(unsigned char *m, const unsigned char *c, unsigned long long clen, const unsigned char *pk, const unsigned char *sk);
functions.description: Decrypts and verifies a ciphertext produced by crypto_box_seal() using the recipient's keypair, writing the plaintext to m.
requirements: m must point to a buffer of size clen - crypto_box_sealbytes().
c must be non-NULL and of length clen, where clen >= crypto_box_sealbytes().
pk must be non-NULL and exactly crypto_box_publickeybytes() bytes.
sk must be non-NULL and exactly crypto_box_secretkeybytes() bytes.
c, pk, sk must be non-NULL (nonnull(2,4,5)).
Return value must be checked (warn_unused_result). On failure, returns -1 and m must be considered uninitialized/invalid.
Plaintext length (clen - overhead) should not exceed crypto_box_messagebytes_max().

functions.name: crypto_box_zerobytes
functions.description: [Deprecated] Returns the number of leading zero bytes required to pad messages for the legacy NaCl-compatible crypto_box() API.
requirements: No arguments.
Only relevant when using deprecated NaCl padding-based APIs.

functions.name: crypto_box_boxzerobytes
functions.description: [Deprecated] Returns the number of leading zero bytes required to pad ciphertexts for the legacy NaCl-compatible crypto_box() API.
requirements: No arguments.
Only relevant when using deprecated NaCl padding-based APIs.

functions.name: crypto_box
functions.signature: int crypto_box(unsigned char *c, const unsigned char *m, unsigned long long mlen, const unsigned char *n, const unsigned char *pk, const unsigned char *sk);
functions.description: [Deprecated; NaCl compatibility] Encrypts/authenticates a padded message m and writes a padded ciphertext c. This API requires zero-padding as per NaCl.
requirements: Deprecated API; prefer crypto_box_easy().
c must point to a buffer of size mlen (NaCl API uses in-place sizes with padding).
m must be padded with crypto_box_zerobytes() leading zero bytes; c must be padded with crypto_box_boxzerobytes() leading zero bytes (per comment: Requires padding).
n must be non-NULL and exactly crypto_box_noncebytes() bytes.
pk must be non-NULL and exactly crypto_box_publickeybytes() bytes.
sk must be non-NULL and exactly crypto_box_secretkeybytes() bytes.
Pointers c, n, pk, sk must be non-NULL (nonnull(1,4,5,6)).
Return value must be checked (warn_unused_result). On failure, non-zero is returned.
Total message length, including padding, should not exceed crypto_box_messagebytes_max() plus required zeros.

functions.name: crypto_box_open
functions.signature: int crypto_box_open(unsigned char *m, const unsigned char *c, unsigned long long clen, const unsigned char *n, const unsigned char *pk, const unsigned char *sk);
functions.description: [Deprecated; NaCl compatibility] Verifies/decrypts a padded ciphertext c into a padded message m. Requires NaCl-style zero-padding.
requirements: Deprecated API; prefer crypto_box_open_easy().
m must point to a buffer of size clen (NaCl API uses in-place sizes with padding).

pk must be non-NULL and exactly crypto_box_publickeybytes() bytes.

Pointers c, n, pk, sk must be non-NULL (nonnull(2,4,5,6)).
Return value must be checked (warn_unused_result). On authentication failure, returns -1 and m must be considered invalid.

functions.name: crypto_box_afternm
functions.signature: int crypto_box_afternm(unsigned char *c, const unsigned char *m, unsigned long long mlen, const unsigned char *n, const unsigned char *k);
functions.description: [Deprecated; NaCl compatibility] Encrypts/authenticates a padded message using a precomputed shared key k. Requires NaCl-style zero-padding.
requirements: Deprecated API; prefer crypto_box_easy_afternm().
c must point to a buffer sized for the padded NaCl interface.
m must be padded with crypto_box_zerobytes() leading zeros; c must be padded with crypto_box_boxzerobytes() leading zeros.
n must be non-NULL and exactly crypto_box_noncebytes() bytes.
k must be non-NULL and exactly crypto_box_beforenmbytes() bytes.
c, n, k must be non-NULL (nonnull(1,4,5)).
Return value should be checked. 0 indicates success; non-zero indicates failure.

functions.name: crypto_box_open_afternm
functions.signature: int crypto_box_open_afternm(unsigned char *m, const unsigned char *c, unsigned long long clen, const unsigned char *n, const unsigned char *k);
functions.description: [Deprecated; NaCl compatibility] Verifies/decrypts a padded ciphertext using a precomputed shared key k. Requires NaCl-style zero-padding.
requirements: Deprecated API; prefer crypto_box_open_easy_afternm().
m must point to a buffer sized for the padded NaCl interface.
c must be padded with crypto_box_boxzerobytes() leading zeros; m must be padded with crypto_box_zerobytes() leading zeros.
n must be non-NULL and exactly crypto_box_noncebytes() bytes.

Return value must be checked (warn_unused_result). On authentication failure, returns -1 and m must be considered invalid.

functions.name: crypto_box_curve25519xchacha20poly1305_seedbytes
functions.description: Returns the size in bytes of a seed suitable for deterministic key pair generation for the Curve25519-XChaCha20-Poly1305 box construction. Typical usage: allocate a buffer of this size and pass it to crypto_box_curve25519xchacha20poly1305_seed_keypair.

functions.name: crypto_box_curve25519xchacha20poly1305_publickeybytes
functions.description: Returns the size in bytes of a public key for the Curve25519-XChaCha20-Poly1305 box construction. Use this to size buffers for public keys.

functions.name: crypto_box_curve25519xchacha20poly1305_secretkeybytes
functions.description: Returns the size in bytes of a secret (private) key for the Curve25519-XChaCha20-Poly1305 box construction. Use this to size buffers for secret keys.

functions.name: crypto_box_curve25519xchacha20poly1305_beforenmbytes
functions.description: Returns the size in bytes of a precomputed shared key produced by the beforenm/precomputation interface. Use this to size buffers passed as the shared key (k) to *_afternm functions.

functions.name: crypto_box_curve25519xchacha20poly1305_noncebytes
functions.description: Returns the size in bytes of a nonce for the Curve25519-XChaCha20-Poly1305 box construction. Allocate nonces of this size; nonces must be unique per (sender secret key, receiver public key) pair.

functions.name: crypto_box_curve25519xchacha20poly1305_macbytes
functions.description: Returns the size in bytes of the authentication tag (MAC) added by the box construction. For the easy interface, ciphertext length = message length + MAC bytes; for the detached interface, the MAC is written separately and has this size.

functions.name: crypto_box_curve25519xchacha20poly1305_messagebytes_max
functions.description: Returns the maximum supported message length (in bytes) for this construction, accounting for the underlying XChaCha20 stream limit minus the MAC length. Use this to cap input lengths.

functions.name: crypto_box_curve25519xchacha20poly1305_seed_keypair
functions.signature: int crypto_box_curve25519xchacha20poly1305_seed_keypair(unsigned char *pk, unsigned char *sk, const unsigned char *seed);
functions.description: Deterministically derives a public/secret key pair from a caller-provided seed for the Curve25519-XChaCha20-Poly1305 box construction. Use when you need reproducible key pairs from a fixed seed. Returns 0 on success; failure codes follow libsodium conventions (inferred).
requirements: pk must point to a writable buffer of size crypto_box_curve25519xchacha20poly1305_PUBLICKEYBYTES (32).
sk must point to a writable buffer of size crypto_box_curve25519xchacha20poly1305_SECRETKEYBYTES (32).
seed must point to a readable buffer of size crypto_box_curve25519xchacha20poly1305_SEEDBYTES (32).

functions.name: crypto_onetimeauth
functions.signature: int crypto_onetimeauth(unsigned char *out, const unsigned char *in, unsigned long long inlen, const unsigned char *k);
functions.description: Computes a one-time authentication tag (MAC) of the message buffer in[0..inlen-1] using the secret key k and writes the tag to out. This is the single-shot (non-incremental) Poly1305 interface.
requirements: out must be a non-null pointer (attribute nonnull(1)).
out must reference a writable buffer of at least crypto_onetimeauth_BYTES bytes (size requirement inferred from API naming and macros).
k must be a non-null pointer (attribute nonnull(4)).
k must reference at least crypto_onetimeauth_KEYBYTES bytes (size requirement inferred from API naming and macros).
in may be NULL only if inlen == 0 (inference from the absence of a nonnull attribute on the input pointer).
The return value should be checked; success/failure semantics are library-defined (commonly 0 on success).

functions.description: Verifies that the authentication tag h matches the MAC of message buffer in[0..inlen-1] under key k. This is the single-shot verification function for Poly1305.
requirements: h must be a non-null pointer (attribute nonnull(1)).
h must reference a buffer containing exactly crypto_onetimeauth_BYTES bytes (size requirement inferred from API naming and macros).
k must be a non-null pointer (attribute nonnull(4)).
k must reference at least crypto_onetimeauth_KEYBYTES bytes (size requirement inferred from API naming and macros).
in may be NULL only if inlen == 0 (inference from the absence of a nonnull attribute on the input pointer).
The function is marked warn_unused_result; callers must check the return value and must not ignore it.

functions.name: crypto_onetimeauth_init
functions.description: Initializes an incremental Poly1305 authentication state with the provided secret key for subsequent update/final calls.
requirements: state must be a non-null pointer to a writable crypto_onetimeauth_state object (attribute nonnull).
key must be a non-null pointer (attribute nonnull).
key must reference at least crypto_onetimeauth_KEYBYTES bytes (size requirement inferred from API naming and macros).
Must be called before any corresponding crypto_onetimeauth_update and crypto_onetimeauth_final that use the same state (sequence requirement inferred from function naming).

functions.name: crypto_onetimeauth_update
functions.signature: int crypto_onetimeauth_update(crypto_onetimeauth_state *state, const unsigned char *in, unsigned long long inlen);
functions.description: Feeds message data to an initialized Poly1305 state. May be called zero or more times before finalizing to process the entire message in chunks.
requirements: state must be a non-null pointer to an initialized crypto_onetimeauth_state (attribute nonnull(1)); the state must have been initialized by crypto_onetimeauth_init (sequence requirement inferred from function naming).
in may be NULL only if inlen == 0 (inference from the absence of a nonnull attribute on the input pointer).

functions.name: crypto_onetimeauth_final
functions.description: Finalizes the incremental Poly1305 computation, writing the authentication tag to out and completing the operation for the given state.
requirements: state must be a non-null pointer to an initialized crypto_onetimeauth_state (attribute nonnull).
out must be a non-null pointer (attribute nonnull).
out must reference a writable buffer of at least crypto_onetimeauth_BYTES bytes (size requirement inferred from API naming and macros).
Must be called after crypto_onetimeauth_init and any crypto_onetimeauth_update calls for the same state (sequence requirement inferred from function naming).

functions.signature: int crypto_onetimeauth_poly1305(unsigned char *out, const unsigned char *in, unsigned long long inlen, const unsigned char *k);
functions.description: Computes a Poly1305 one-time authentication tag over the message buffer in (length inlen) using the 32-byte key k, storing the 16-byte tag into out. Intended for one-shot (non-streaming) MAC computation.
requirements: out must be non-NULL and point to a writable buffer of at least crypto_onetimeauth_poly1305_BYTES (16) bytes.
k must be non-NULL and point to a buffer of exactly crypto_onetimeauth_poly1305_KEYBYTES (32) bytes.
If inlen > 0, in must be non-NULL; in may be NULL only when inlen == 0 (inferred from nonnull attribute only applying to out and k).
The function returns 0 on success; callers should handle non-zero returns as errors (inferred from libsodium conventions).
The same key must not be reused with unrelated protocols; the key must be treated as secret (inferred from Poly1305 usage).

functions.signature: int crypto_onetimeauth_poly1305_verify(const unsigned char *h, const unsigned char *in, unsigned long long inlen, const unsigned char *k);
functions.description: Verifies that the authentication tag h is a valid Poly1305 MAC for the message buffer in (length inlen) under the key k. Performs a constant-time comparison. Returns 0 if the verification succeeds, and a non-zero value (typically -1) otherwise. The warn_unused_result attribute indicates callers must check the return value.
requirements: h must be non-NULL and point to a buffer of at least crypto_onetimeauth_poly1305_BYTES (16) bytes.
k must be non-NULL and point to a buffer of exactly crypto_onetimeauth_poly1305_KEYBYTES (32) bytes.
If inlen > 0, in must be non-NULL; in may be NULL only when inlen == 0 (inferred from nonnull attribute not applying to in).
Callers must check and handle the return value (warn_unused_result).
Do not use the result unless verification returns 0; on failure, callers must treat the data as unauthenticated (inferred from verify semantics).

functions.name: crypto_onetimeauth_poly1305_init
functions.description: Initializes a streaming Poly1305 state with the 32-byte key. Must be called before update/final to compute a MAC incrementally.
requirements: state must be non-NULL and point to a valid, writable crypto_onetimeauth_poly1305_state object (alignment is provided by the type).
key must be non-NULL and point to a buffer of exactly crypto_onetimeauth_poly1305_KEYBYTES (32) bytes.
Must be called before any corresponding crypto_onetimeauth_poly1305_update and crypto_onetimeauth_poly1305_final on the same state.

functions.name: crypto_onetimeauth_poly1305_update
functions.signature: int crypto_onetimeauth_poly1305_update(crypto_onetimeauth_poly1305_state *state, const unsigned char *in, unsigned long long inlen);
functions.description: Feeds a chunk of message data into the streaming Poly1305 state previously initialized with crypto_onetimeauth_poly1305_init. Can be called zero or more times before final.
requirements: state must be non-NULL and must have been initialized with crypto_onetimeauth_poly1305_init.
If inlen > 0, in must be non-NULL; in may be NULL only when inlen == 0 (inferred).
May be called multiple times; the order of calls defines the message being authenticated.
Must be followed by crypto_onetimeauth_poly1305_final to obtain the authentication tag before the state is reused or discarded.

functions.name: crypto_onetimeauth_poly1305_final
functions.description: Finalizes the streaming Poly1305 computation and writes the 16-byte authentication tag to out. After finalizing, the state should not be used again unless reinitialized.
requirements: state must be non-NULL and must have been initialized with crypto_onetimeauth_poly1305_init (and optionally updated).
out must be non-NULL and point to a writable buffer of at least crypto_onetimeauth_poly1305_BYTES (16) bytes.

Should be called exactly once per initialized state, after all desired crypto_onetimeauth_poly1305_update calls and before reinitializing or discarding the state (inferred from streaming MAC semantics).

functions.name: crypto_onetimeauth_poly1305_keygen
functions.description: Generates a new random 32-byte key suitable for Poly1305 and writes it to k. Convenience for obtaining a uniformly random secret key.

functions.name: crypto_pwhash
functions.signature: SODIUM_EXPORT int crypto_pwhash(unsigned char * const out, unsigned long long outlen, const char * const passwd, unsigned long long passwdlen, const unsigned char * const salt, unsigned long long opslimit, size_t memlimit, int alg) __attribute__ ((warn_unused_result)) __attribute__ ((nonnull));
functions.description: Computes a password hash using the specified algorithm and parameters. Writes outlen bytes to out using the password bytes (passwd, passwdlen), a salt, an opslimit (work factor), a memlimit (memory usage), and an algorithm identifier (alg). Intended for deriving keys or storing fixed-length password hashes. Note: per the header comment, if you need deterministic verification, store all parameters including the algorithm identifier because defaults may change.
requirements: out must point to a writable buffer of at least outlen bytes (nonnull).
outlen must be within [crypto_pwhash_bytes_min(), crypto_pwhash_bytes_max()].
passwd must be a non-null pointer to passwdlen bytes; passwdlen must be within [crypto_pwhash_passwd_min(), crypto_pwhash_passwd_max()].
salt must be a non-null pointer to a buffer of exactly crypto_pwhash_saltbytes() bytes.
opslimit must be within [crypto_pwhash_opslimit_min(), crypto_pwhash_opslimit_max()].
memlimit must be within [crypto_pwhash_memlimit_min(), crypto_pwhash_memlimit_max()].
alg must be a valid algorithm id (e.g., crypto_pwhash_alg_default(), crypto_pwhash_alg_argon2id13(), crypto_pwhash_alg_argon2i13()).
All pointer parameters are annotated nonnull; do not pass NULL.
The return value is annotated warn_unused_result; callers must check for success/failure before using the output.
If deterministic verification across versions is needed, the caller must store all parameters used, including alg, opslimit, and memlimit.

functions.name: crypto_pwhash_str

functions.description: Computes a password hash string that encodes the algorithm and parameters along with the hash, writing a NUL-terminated string into out. This string is sufficient to verify a password later with crypto_pwhash_str_verify; it includes the algorithm identifier and parameters.

functions.name: crypto_pwhash_scryptsalsa208sha256_str_verify
