functions.description: Verifies that an encoded scrypt-salsa208-sha256 hash string matches the supplied password. Intended for password authentication against a stored hash produced by crypto_pwhash_scryptsalsa208sha256_str.
requirements: str must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated string produced by crypto_pwhash_scryptsalsa208sha256_str and typically start with crypto_pwhash_scryptsalsa208sha256_strprefix() (nonnull attribute).
passwd may contain arbitrary bytes and is not required to be NUL-terminated; must be non-NULL if passwdlen > 0 (nonnull attribute applies).
The return value must be checked (warn_unused_result): 0 indicates verification success; non-zero indicates mismatch or error (inferred from libsodium conventions).

functions.name: crypto_pwhash_scryptsalsa208sha256_ll
functions.signature: int crypto_pwhash_scryptsalsa208sha256_ll(const uint8_t * passwd, size_t passwdlen, const uint8_t * salt, size_t saltlen, uint64_t N, uint32_t r, uint32_t p, uint8_t * buf, size_t buflen);
functions.description: Low-level scrypt key derivation function. Derives buflen bytes into buf from passwd and salt using parameters N, r, and p. Exposes raw scrypt parameters and accepts arbitrary salt length. Intended for expert use when full control over scrypt parameters is required.
requirements: passwd must be a non-NULL pointer to a buffer of length passwdlen (nonnull attribute).
salt must be a non-NULL pointer to a buffer of length saltlen (nonnull attribute).
buf must be a non-NULL pointer to a writable buffer of at least buflen bytes (nonnull attribute).

N, r, and p are the scrypt cost parameters; callers should choose values consistent with scrypt requirements (e.g., N >= 2 and a power of two; r >= 1; p >= 1). These constraints are standard for scrypt but exact enforcement is implementation-defined (inferred from scrypt).
The return value must be checked (warn_unused_result): 0 indicates success; non-zero indicates failure (inferred from libsodium conventions).

functions.name: crypto_pwhash_scryptsalsa208sha256_str_needs_rehash
functions.signature: int crypto_pwhash_scryptsalsa208sha256_str_needs_rehash(const char * str, unsigned long long opslimit, size_t memlimit);
functions.description: Checks whether an encoded hash string was created with parameters weaker than the provided opslimit and memlimit, indicating it should be rehashed. Useful when increasing security parameters over time.
requirements: str must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated hash string produced by crypto_pwhash_scryptsalsa208sha256_str (nonnull attribute).
opslimit and memlimit should be valid values within this API’s min/max bounds to reflect the desired current policy.
The return value must be checked (warn_unused_result): returns 1 if rehash is needed, 0 if not, negative on error (inferred from libsodium conventions).

functions.name: crypto_scalarmult_bytes
functions.description: Returns the size in bytes of a group element/output produced by the crypto_scalarmult primitive (currently curve25519). Use this to size output buffers for results such as q.

functions.name: crypto_scalarmult_scalarbytes
functions.description: Returns the size in bytes of a scalar (the private/secret multiplier) accepted by the crypto_scalarmult primitive (currently curve25519). Use this to size scalar input buffers such as n.

functions.name: crypto_scalarmult_primitive
functions.description: Returns the name of the underlying primitive as a NUL-terminated string ("curve25519"). Useful for runtime introspection or diagnostics.

functions.name: crypto_scalarmult_base
functions.signature: int crypto_scalarmult_base(unsigned char *q, const unsigned char *n) __attribute__ ((nonnull));
functions.description: Computes q = n * base_point for the configured primitive (curve25519), i.e., derives a public key q from a secret scalar n. Typical use: generate a Curve25519 public key from a secret scalar.
requirements: q must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to a writable buffer of exactly crypto_scalarmult_BYTES bytes (inferred from API naming and family).
n must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to a readable buffer of exactly crypto_scalarmult_SCALARBYTES bytes (inferred from API naming and family).
All pointer arguments are required to be non-NULL (nonnull attribute).
The return value must be checked by the caller if failure is possible; exact success/error codes are not specified here (unknown).

functions.name: crypto_scalarmult
functions.signature: int crypto_scalarmult(unsigned char *q, const unsigned char *n, const unsigned char *p) __attribute__ ((warn_unused_result)) __attribute__ ((nonnull));
functions.description: Computes q = n * p for the configured primitive (curve25519), i.e., scalar-multiplies a public group element p by a secret scalar n to produce q (used for Diffie–Hellman style shared secrets). Note: Do not use q directly as a shared key; hash the result together with both public keys to derive a secret (e.g., H(q || client_pk || server_pk)) or use the crypto_kx() API.
requirements: q must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to a writable buffer of exactly crypto_scalarmult_BYTES bytes (inferred from API naming and family).
n must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to a readable buffer of exactly crypto_scalarmult_SCALARBYTES bytes (inferred from API naming and family).
p must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to a readable buffer of exactly crypto_scalarmult_BYTES bytes (inferred from API naming and family).
All pointer arguments are required to be non-NULL (nonnull attribute).

The function’s return value must be used/checked by the caller (warn_unused_result). The specific success/error conventions are not stated here; treat any non-zero (or negative) return as an error unless documented elsewhere (unknown exact semantics).
Callers must not use the raw q output directly as a shared key; derive a key by hashing q with both public keys as documented, or use crypto_kx().

functions.name: crypto_scalarmult_curve25519_bytes
functions.description: Returns the size in bytes of Curve25519 scalar-multiplication outputs (Montgomery u-coordinate). Typically 32 bytes. Use this to size output buffers for crypto_scalarmult_curve25519() and related APIs.
requirements: No arguments required.
Caller should use the returned value to allocate/validate output buffer sizes for related functions.

functions.name: crypto_scalarmult_curve25519_scalarbytes
functions.description: Returns the size in bytes of Curve25519 scalars (secret keys). Typically 32 bytes. Use this to size/validate scalar inputs for scalar-multiplication functions.
requirements: No arguments required.
Caller should use the returned value to allocate/validate scalar buffer sizes for related functions.

functions.name: crypto_scalarmult_curve25519
functions.signature: int crypto_scalarmult_curve25519(unsigned char *q, const unsigned char *n, const unsigned char *p) __attribute__((warn_unused_result)) __attribute__((nonnull));
functions.description: Computes the Curve25519 scalar multiplication q = n * p, where n is a 32-byte scalar and p is a 32-byte Curve25519 point (Montgomery u-coordinate). Intended for deriving a shared secret from a private scalar and a peer public key. Do not use the raw result directly for key exchange; instead, hash the result together with both public keys (e.g., H(q || client_pk || server_pk)) or use the higher-level crypto_kx() API. Returns an int status; the exact success/error convention is not specified in this header—callers must check the return value.
requirements: q must point to a writable buffer of at least crypto_scalarmult_curve25519_BYTES (32) bytes.
n must point to a readable buffer of exactly crypto_scalarmult_curve25519_SCALARBYTES (32) bytes.
p must point to a readable buffer of exactly crypto_scalarmult_curve25519_BYTES (32) bytes.
q, n, and p must be non-null (function is annotated nonnull).
The return value must be checked (function is annotated warn_unused_result).
Do not use the raw output directly for key exchange; hash it with both public keys (e.g., H(q || client_pk || server_pk)) or use crypto_kx().
Callers must ensure provided buffers are properly initialized to the required lengths before calling.

Thread-safety and error code semantics are not specified in this header; callers should handle any nonzero/negative return as an error according to the library’s documentation (details unknown in this header).

functions.name: crypto_scalarmult_curve25519_base
functions.description: Computes the public key q = n * basepoint for Curve25519 (X25519) given a 32-byte secret scalar n. Used to derive a public key from a secret key. Returns an int status; exact success/error convention is not specified in this header—callers should check the return value.
requirements: q must point to a writable buffer of at least crypto_scalarmult_curve25519_BYTES (32) bytes.
n must point to a readable buffer of exactly crypto_scalarmult_curve25519_SCALARBYTES (32) bytes.
q and n must be non-null (function is annotated nonnull).
Callers should check the return value and handle errors according to the library’s documentation (details unknown in this header).
Callers must ensure provided buffers are properly initialized to the required lengths before calling.

functions.name: crypto_scalarmult_ed25519_bytes
functions.description: Returns the size, in bytes, of Ed25519 group elements produced/consumed by crypto_scalarmult_ed25519* APIs. Typically 32 bytes.
requirements: No arguments; can be called at any time.
Return value should be used to size buffers for points (q and p).

functions.name: crypto_scalarmult_ed25519_scalarbytes
functions.description: Returns the size, in bytes, of scalars used by crypto_scalarmult_ed25519* APIs. Typically 32 bytes.
requirements: No arguments; can be called at any time.
Return value should be used to size buffers for scalars (n).

functions.name: crypto_scalarmult_ed25519
functions.signature: int crypto_scalarmult_ed25519(unsigned char *q, const unsigned char *n, const unsigned char *p) __attribute__ ((warn_unused_result)) __attribute__ ((nonnull));
functions.description: Computes the scalar multiplication q = n * p on the Ed25519 curve with clamping applied to the scalar n (per Ed25519 rules). Intended for deriving a shared point or performing general group scalar multiplication. The result must not be used directly for key exchange; hash the result together with both public keys, or use the crypto_kx() API.
requirements: q must be a non-null pointer to a writable buffer of at least crypto_scalarmult_ed25519_bytes() (32) bytes.
n must be a non-null pointer to a buffer of exactly crypto_scalarmult_ed25519_scalarbytes() (32) bytes containing the scalar. The scalar is clamped internally.
p must be a non-null pointer to a buffer of exactly crypto_scalarmult_ed25519_bytes() (32) bytes containing an encoded Ed25519 group element (public point).
Caller must check the return value (warn_unused_result). Return code conventions are library-defined; in libsodium patterns, 0 indicates success and non-zero indicates failure.
Do not use q directly for key exchange. If used for key agreement, hash as H(q || client_pk || server_pk) or use the crypto_kx() API instead (as explicitly noted in the header).

functions.name: crypto_scalarmult_ed25519_noclamp
functions.signature: int crypto_scalarmult_ed25519_noclamp(unsigned char *q, const unsigned char *n, const unsigned char *p) __attribute__ ((warn_unused_result)) __attribute__ ((nonnull));
functions.description: Computes the scalar multiplication q = n * p on the Ed25519 curve without clamping the scalar n. Use when you need raw scalar multiplication semantics (e.g., when n is already prepared or for protocols that define their own scalar format). The result must not be used directly for key exchange; hash the result together with both public keys, or use the crypto_kx() API.
requirements: q must be a non-null pointer to a writable buffer of at least crypto_scalarmult_ed25519_bytes() (32) bytes.

n must be a non-null pointer to a buffer of exactly crypto_scalarmult_ed25519_scalarbytes() (32) bytes containing the scalar. No clamping is performed; caller is responsible for providing a valid/appropriate scalar for their protocol.
p must be a non-null pointer to a buffer of exactly crypto_scalarmult_ed25519_bytes() (32) bytes containing an encoded Ed25519 group element (public point).
Caller must check the return value (warn_unused_result). Return code conventions are library-defined; in libsodium patterns, 0 indicates success and non-zero indicates failure.
Do not use q directly for key exchange. If used for key agreement, hash as H(q || client_pk || server_pk) or use the crypto_kx() API instead (as explicitly noted in the header).

functions.name: crypto_scalarmult_ed25519_base
functions.signature: int crypto_scalarmult_ed25519_base(unsigned char *q, const unsigned char *n) __attribute__ ((nonnull));
functions.description: Computes the scalar multiplication of the Ed25519 base point by the clamped scalar n, producing the public point q (i.e., q = n * basepoint). Commonly used to derive a public key from a private scalar.
requirements: q must be a non-null pointer to a writable buffer of at least crypto_scalarmult_ed25519_bytes() (32) bytes.
n must be a non-null pointer to a buffer of exactly crypto_scalarmult_ed25519_scalarbytes() (32) bytes containing the scalar. The scalar is clamped internally.
Caller should check the integer return value for success/failure; exact return conventions are library-defined (commonly 0 on success, non-zero on failure).

functions.name: crypto_scalarmult_ed25519_base_noclamp
functions.description: Computes the scalar multiplication of the Ed25519 base point by the raw scalar n without applying clamping (q = n * basepoint). Use when you need base point multiplication with an already-prepared or protocol-defined scalar.
requirements: q must be a non-null pointer to a writable buffer of at least crypto_scalarmult_ed25519_bytes() (32) bytes.

n must be a non-null pointer to a buffer of exactly crypto_scalarmult_ed25519_scalarbytes() (32) bytes containing the scalar. No clamping is performed; caller is responsible for providing a valid/appropriate scalar for their protocol.
Caller should check the integer return value for success/failure; exact return conventions are library-defined (commonly 0 on success, non-zero on failure).

functions.name: crypto_scalarmult_ristretto255_bytes
functions.description: Returns the size in bytes of a Ristretto255 group element produced by this API. This value is constant (32 bytes) and can be used to size output buffers for group elements (e.g., q). Typical usage: allocate an output buffer of this size before calling scalar-multiplication functions.
requirements: No arguments; may be called at any time.
Caller should use the returned size to allocate buffers for group elements (e.g., q) to avoid undersized buffers.

functions.name: crypto_scalarmult_ristretto255_scalarbytes
functions.description: Returns the size in bytes of a scalar for Ristretto255 used by this API. This value is constant (32 bytes) and can be used to size buffers for scalars (e.g., n). Typical usage: allocate or validate scalar inputs using this size.
requirements: No arguments; may be called at any time.
Caller should use the returned size to allocate/validate scalar buffers (e.g., n).

functions.name: crypto_scalarmult_ristretto255
functions.signature: int crypto_scalarmult_ristretto255(unsigned char *q, const unsigned char *n, const unsigned char *p) __attribute__ ((warn_unused_result)) __attribute__ ((nonnull));
functions.description: Computes a Ristretto255 scalar multiplication q = n * p, where n is a 32-byte scalar and p is a 32-byte encoded Ristretto255 group element. On success, writes the 32-byte encoded group element to q and returns 0; on invalid input (e.g., an invalid encoding of p), returns -1. Note: Do not use the raw result directly for key exchange; instead, hash the result together with both public keys (e.g., H(q || client_pk || server_pk)) or use the crypto_kx() API.
requirements: q must be a non-NULL pointer to a writable buffer of at least crypto_scalarmult_ristretto255_BYTES (32) bytes.
n must be a non-NULL pointer to a buffer of exactly crypto_scalarmult_ristretto255_SCALARBYTES (32) bytes representing the scalar.
p must be a non-NULL pointer to a buffer of exactly crypto_scalarmult_ristretto255_BYTES (32) bytes containing a valid encoded Ristretto255 group element.
The function may fail (returns -1) if inputs are invalid (e.g., invalid point encoding); callers must check the return value (warn_unused_result) and must not use q on failure.
The direct output must not be used as a shared secret for key exchange; callers must hash the result with both public keys as described in the header comment or use crypto_kx().

functions.name: crypto_scalarmult_ristretto255_base
functions.description: Computes q = n * B, the scalar multiplication of the standard Ristretto255 base point B by the 32-byte scalar n. On success, writes the 32-byte encoded group element (public key) to q and returns 0. This is typically used to derive a public key from a secret scalar. As with other scalarmult results, do not use the raw result directly for key exchange; hash appropriately or use crypto_kx().
requirements: q must be a non-NULL pointer to a writable buffer of at least crypto_scalarmult_ristretto255_BYTES (32) bytes.
n must be a non-NULL pointer to a buffer of exactly crypto_scalarmult_ristretto255_SCALARBYTES (32) bytes representing the scalar.
Callers should check the return value; on error, q must be considered undefined.
The direct output must not be used as a shared secret for key exchange; callers must hash the result with both public keys or use crypto_kx().

functions.name: crypto_secretbox_keybytes
functions.description: Returns the size in bytes of a secretbox key for the current primitive (XSalsa20-Poly1305). Typically used to allocate or validate key buffers.
requirements: No arguments; simply call to retrieve the required key length.
Use the returned size to allocate key buffers for other crypto_secretbox functions.

functions.name: crypto_secretbox_noncebytes
functions.description: Returns the size in bytes of a nonce for the secretbox primitive. Use to allocate or validate nonces.
requirements: No arguments; simply call to retrieve the required nonce length.
Use the returned size to allocate nonce buffers for crypto_secretbox operations.

functions.name: crypto_secretbox_macbytes
functions.description: Returns the size in bytes of the authentication tag (MAC) added by secretbox_easy or produced/consumed by the detached API.
requirements: No arguments; call to obtain MAC length for buffer sizing.
Ensure ciphertext buffers account for this many extra bytes when using the _easy API.

functions.name: crypto_secretbox_primitive
functions.description: Returns the name of the underlying authenticated-encryption primitive as a NUL-terminated string ("xsalsa20poly1305"). Useful for diagnostics or capability checks.
requirements: No arguments; returned pointer is to a static string that must not be modified or freed.

functions.name: crypto_secretbox_messagebytes_max
functions.description: Returns the maximum supported message size in bytes for crypto_secretbox. Use to validate inputs before encryption/decryption.
requirements: No arguments; use the returned limit to validate message lengths.
Do not attempt to encrypt messages larger than the returned maximum.

functions.name: crypto_secretbox_easy
functions.signature: int crypto_secretbox_easy(unsigned char *c, const unsigned char *m, unsigned long long mlen, const unsigned char *n, const unsigned char *k) __attribute__ ((nonnull(1, 4, 5)));
functions.description: Authenticated encryption (secretbox) using XSalsa20-Poly1305. Encrypts message m (mlen bytes) using nonce n and key k, writing MAC||ciphertext to c. Returns 0 on success.
requirements: c must be non-null and point to a buffer of at least mlen + crypto_secretbox_macbytes() bytes.
m may be null only when mlen == 0; otherwise it should point to mlen bytes of plaintext.
n must be non-null and point to crypto_secretbox_noncebytes() bytes.
k must be non-null and point to crypto_secretbox_keybytes() bytes.
Do not reuse a nonce n with the same key k (nonce must be unique per key).
mlen must be <= crypto_secretbox_messagebytes_max().
Function returns 0 on success; no negative error codes are used for encryption.

functions.name: crypto_secretbox_open_easy
functions.signature: int crypto_secretbox_open_easy(unsigned char *m, const unsigned char *c, unsigned long long clen, const unsigned char *n, const unsigned char *k) __attribute__ ((warn_unused_result)) __attribute__ ((nonnull(2, 4, 5)));
functions.description: Verifies and decrypts a secretbox created with crypto_secretbox_easy. Given c (MAC||ciphertext) of length clen, nonce n, and key k, writes plaintext to m and returns 0 on success, -1 on authentication failure.
requirements: c must be non-null and point to clen bytes containing MAC||ciphertext.
m may be null only when clen == crypto_secretbox_macbytes(); otherwise it must point to a buffer of at least (clen - crypto_secretbox_macbytes()) bytes.
clen must be >= crypto_secretbox_macbytes().
n must be non-null and point to crypto_secretbox_noncebytes() bytes.
k must be non-null and point to crypto_secretbox_keybytes() bytes.
The ciphertext must have been produced with the same primitive and the same key; nonce must match the one used for encryption.
Return value must be checked (warn_unused_result): 0 indicates success; -1 indicates verification failed and no plaintext should be used.
Do not reuse a nonce n with the same key k for new encryptions.

functions.name: crypto_secretbox_detached
functions.signature: int crypto_secretbox_detached(unsigned char *c, unsigned char *mac, const unsigned char *m, unsigned long long mlen, const unsigned char *n, const unsigned char *k) __attribute__ ((nonnull(1, 2, 5, 6)));
functions.description: Authenticated encryption (detached mode). Encrypts message m (mlen bytes) with nonce n and key k. Writes ciphertext to c and the authentication tag to mac. Returns 0 on success.
requirements: c must be non-null and point to a buffer of at least mlen bytes.
mac must be non-null and point to a buffer of at least crypto_secretbox_macbytes() bytes.
m may be null only when mlen == 0; otherwise it should point to mlen bytes of plaintext.
n must be non-null and point to crypto_secretbox_noncebytes() bytes.
k must be non-null and point to crypto_secretbox_keybytes() bytes.
Do not reuse a nonce n with the same key k.
mlen must be <= crypto_secretbox_messagebytes_max().
Returns 0 on success.

functions.name: crypto_secretbox_open_detached
functions.signature: int crypto_secretbox_open_detached(unsigned char *m, const unsigned char *c, const unsigned char *mac, unsigned long long clen, const unsigned char *n, const unsigned char *k) __attribute__ ((warn_unused_result)) __attribute__ ((nonnull(2, 3, 5, 6)));
functions.description: Verifies and decrypts data encrypted with crypto_secretbox_detached. Given ciphertext c (clen bytes), MAC mac, nonce n, and key k, writes plaintext to m and returns 0 on success, -1 on authentication failure.
requirements: c must be non-null and point to clen bytes of ciphertext.
mac must be non-null and point to crypto_secretbox_macbytes() bytes.
m may be null only when clen == 0; otherwise it must point to a buffer of at least clen bytes.
n must be non-null and point to crypto_secretbox_noncebytes() bytes.
k must be non-null and point to crypto_secretbox_keybytes() bytes.
Return value must be checked (warn_unused_result): 0 indicates success; -1 indicates verification failed and no plaintext should be used.
Do not reuse a nonce n with the same key k for new encryptions.

functions.name: crypto_secretbox_keygen
functions.description: Generates a new random key suitable for crypto_secretbox operations and writes it to k.
requirements: k must be non-null and point to a buffer of at least crypto_secretbox_keybytes() bytes.
The generated key should be treated as secret and stored securely.
Do not reuse keys with non-unique nonces.
The function does not return a value; callers should assume it always succeeds under normal circumstances.

functions.name: crypto_secretbox_zerobytes
functions.description: Deprecated NaCl-compatible API constant accessor. Returns the required number of leading zero bytes that plaintext must be padded with when using the deprecated crypto_secretbox (padded) interface.
requirements: No arguments; used only with the deprecated padded NaCl-compatible API.
When using the deprecated crypto_secretbox (not _easy), the message buffer must be padded with this many leading zero bytes.

functions.name: crypto_secretbox_boxzerobytes
functions.description: Deprecated NaCl-compatible API constant accessor. Returns the number of leading zero bytes present in the ciphertext when using the deprecated padded crypto_secretbox interface.
requirements: No arguments; used only with the deprecated padded NaCl-compatible API.
When using the deprecated crypto_secretbox (not _easy), the ciphertext buffer will contain this many leading zero bytes.

functions.name: crypto_secretbox
functions.signature: int crypto_secretbox(unsigned char *c, const unsigned char *m, unsigned long long mlen, const unsigned char *n, const unsigned char *k) __attribute__ ((deprecated)) __attribute__ ((nonnull(1, 4, 5)));
functions.description: Deprecated NaCl-compatible padded encryption API. Encrypts padded message m (mlen bytes) using nonce n and key k, writing padded ciphertext to c. Returns 0 on success.
requirements: c must be non-null and point to a buffer of at least mlen bytes.
m must point to mlen bytes and must be padded with crypto_secretbox_zerobytes() leading zeros; mlen must be >= crypto_secretbox_zerobytes().
The first crypto_secretbox_zerobytes() bytes of m must be zero; the corresponding first crypto_secretbox_boxzerobytes() bytes of c will be zero.
n must be non-null and point to crypto_secretbox_noncebytes() bytes.
k must be non-null and point to crypto_secretbox_keybytes() bytes.
Do not reuse a nonce n with the same key k.
Returns 0 on success. This API is deprecated; prefer crypto_secretbox_easy.

functions.name: crypto_secretbox_open
functions.signature: int crypto_secretbox_open(unsigned char *m, const unsigned char *c, unsigned long long clen, const unsigned char *n, const unsigned char *k) __attribute__ ((deprecated)) __attribute__ ((warn_unused_result)) __attribute__ ((nonnull(2, 4, 5)));
functions.description: Deprecated NaCl-compatible padded decryption API. Verifies and decrypts padded ciphertext c (clen bytes) using nonce n and key k, writing padded plaintext to m. Returns 0 on success, -1 on authentication failure.
requirements: c must be non-null and point to clen bytes and must have crypto_secretbox_boxzerobytes() leading zeros; clen must be >= crypto_secretbox_boxzerobytes().
m must point to a buffer of at least clen bytes; the first crypto_secretbox_zerobytes() bytes of the resulting plaintext will be zeros.
n must be non-null and point to crypto_secretbox_noncebytes() bytes.
k must be non-null and point to crypto_secretbox_keybytes() bytes.
Return value must be checked (warn_unused_result): 0 indicates success; -1 indicates verification failed and output must not be used.
Do not reuse a nonce n with the same key k.
This API is deprecated; prefer crypto_secretbox_open_easy.

functions.name: crypto_secretbox_xchacha20poly1305_keybytes
functions.description: Returns the required key size in bytes for XChaCha20-Poly1305 secretbox operations. Expected usage: call to allocate or validate a key buffer length before encryption/decryption. Notes: Corresponds to the macro crypto_secretbox_xchacha20poly1305_KEYBYTES (32).
requirements: No arguments; function is pure and has no side effects.
Use the returned value to size key buffers for related APIs.

functions.name: crypto_secretbox_xchacha20poly1305_noncebytes
functions.description: Returns the required nonce size in bytes for XChaCha20-Poly1305 secretbox operations. Expected usage: call to allocate or validate a nonce buffer length before encryption/decryption. Notes: Corresponds to the macro crypto_secretbox_xchacha20poly1305_NONCEBYTES (24).
requirements: No arguments; function is pure and has no side effects.
Use the returned value to size nonce buffers for related APIs.

functions.name: crypto_secretbox_xchacha20poly1305_macbytes
functions.description: Returns the size in bytes of the authentication tag (MAC) produced/required by XChaCha20-Poly1305 secretbox operations. Expected usage: compute ciphertext or plaintext buffer lengths. Notes: Corresponds to the macro crypto_secretbox_xchacha20poly1305_MACBYTES (16).
requirements: No arguments; function is pure and has no side effects.
Use the returned value when sizing ciphertext (mlen + MACBYTES) or detached MAC buffers.

functions.name: crypto_secretbox_xchacha20poly1305_messagebytes_max
functions.description: Returns the maximum supported plaintext message size (in bytes) for XChaCha20-Poly1305 secretbox operations. Expected usage: validate that mlen does not exceed this limit prior to calling encrypt/decrypt APIs. Notes: Defined as crypto_stream_xchacha20_MESSAGEBYTES_MAX - crypto_secretbox_xchacha20poly1305_MACBYTES.
requirements: No arguments; function is pure and has no side effects.
Callers should ensure mlen <= crypto_secretbox_xchacha20poly1305_messagebytes_max().

functions.name: crypto_secretbox_xchacha20poly1305_easy
functions.signature:
int crypto_secretbox_xchacha20poly1305_easy(unsigned char *c,
                                            const unsigned char *m,
                                            unsigned long long mlen,
                                            const unsigned char *n,
                                            const unsigned char *k) __attribute__ ((nonnull(1, 4, 5)));
functions.description: Encrypts and authenticates a message m of length mlen using key k and nonce n, writing the result to c. Produces a combined ciphertext consisting of a MAC (16 bytes) followed by the encrypted message. Expected usage: allocate c with size mlen + crypto_secretbox_xchacha20poly1305_MACBYTES and pass a 24-byte nonce and 32-byte key. Return value follows libsodium convention: 0 on success; non-zero on error.
requirements: c must be a valid, writable buffer of at least mlen + crypto_secretbox_xchacha20poly1305_MACBYTES bytes (inferred from secretbox API pattern).
n must point to a buffer of exactly crypto_secretbox_xchacha20poly1305_NONCEBYTES bytes (24).
k must point to a buffer of exactly crypto_secretbox_xchacha20poly1305_KEYBYTES bytes (32).

mlen should be <= crypto_secretbox_xchacha20poly1305_messagebytes_max().
Return value must be checked; treat any non-zero as failure (libsodium pattern).
Nonce uniqueness per key is typically required to ensure security (inferred from nonce semantics), but exact policy is not stated in this header.

functions.name: crypto_secretbox_xchacha20poly1305_open_easy
functions.signature:

                                                 const unsigned char *c,
                                                 unsigned long long clen,

functions.description: Verifies and decrypts a combined ciphertext c of length clen produced by crypto_secretbox_xchacha20poly1305_easy, using key k and nonce n, writing the recovered plaintext to m. Expected usage: allocate m with size clen - crypto_secretbox_xchacha20poly1305_MACBYTES and pass the same nonce and key used for encryption. Returns 0 on success and -1 (or non-zero) on authentication failure per libsodium convention; return value is annotated warn_unused_result and must be checked.
requirements: c, n, and k must be non-null (per nonnull(2,4,5) attribute).
clen must be at least crypto_secretbox_xchacha20poly1305_MACBYTES and typically equals mlen + MACBYTES (inferred from secretbox API pattern).
m must be a valid, writable buffer of at least clen - crypto_secretbox_xchacha20poly1305_MACBYTES bytes (inferred).
The return value must be checked; if non-zero, the plaintext in m must not be used (per warn_unused_result and libsodium pattern).
Nonce n must be the same as used for encryption; size is crypto_secretbox_xchacha20poly1305_NONCEBYTES (24).
Key k must be the same key used for encryption; size is crypto_secretbox_xchacha20poly1305_KEYBYTES (32).

functions.name: crypto_secretbox_xchacha20poly1305_detached
functions.signature:
int crypto_secretbox_xchacha20poly1305_detached(unsigned char *c,
                                                unsigned char *mac,
                                                const unsigned char *m,
                                                unsigned long long mlen,
                                                const unsigned char *n,
                                                const unsigned char *k) __attribute__ ((nonnull(1, 2, 5, 6)));
functions.description: Encrypts and authenticates message m of length mlen using key k and nonce n, writing the ciphertext to c and the authentication tag to mac (detached mode). Expected usage: allocate c with size mlen and mac with size crypto_secretbox_xchacha20poly1305_MACBYTES. Returns 0 on success; non-zero on error per libsodium convention.
requirements: c must be a valid, writable buffer of at least mlen bytes (inferred from detached mode semantics).
mac must be a valid, writable buffer of exactly crypto_secretbox_xchacha20poly1305_MACBYTES bytes (16).
n must point to a buffer of exactly crypto_secretbox_xchacha20poly1305_NONCEBYTES bytes (24).
k must point to a buffer of exactly crypto_secretbox_xchacha20poly1305_KEYBYTES bytes (32).
Parameters c, mac, n, and k must be non-null (per nonnull(1,2,5,6) attribute).
mlen should be <= crypto_secretbox_xchacha20poly1305_messagebytes_max().
Nonce uniqueness per key is typically required to ensure security (inferred from nonce semantics), but exact policy is not stated in this header.

functions.name: crypto_secretbox_xchacha20poly1305_open_detached
functions.signature:
int crypto_secretbox_xchacha20poly1305_open_detached(unsigned char *m,
                                                     const unsigned char *c,
