                                                     unsigned long long clen,
                                                     const unsigned char *n,
                                                     const unsigned char *k) __attribute__ ((warn_unused_result)) __attribute__ ((nonnull(2, 3, 5, 6)));
functions.description: Verifies MAC and decrypts ciphertext c of length clen using key k and nonce n, writing plaintext to m; authentication tag is provided separately via mac (detached mode). Expected usage: allocate m with size clen, pass mac of size crypto_secretbox_xchacha20poly1305_MACBYTES. Returns 0 on success and -1 (or non-zero) on authentication failure per libsodium convention; return value is annotated warn_unused_result and must be checked.
requirements: c, mac, n, and k must be non-null (per nonnull(2,3,5,6) attribute).
clen must equal the plaintext length mlen (detached mode; inferred).
m must be a valid, writable buffer of at least clen bytes (inferred).
mac must point to a buffer of exactly crypto_secretbox_xchacha20poly1305_MACBYTES bytes (16).
Nonce n must be the same as used when encrypting; size is crypto_secretbox_xchacha20poly1305_NONCEBYTES (24).
Key k must be the same key used for encryption; size is crypto_secretbox_xchacha20poly1305_KEYBYTES (32).
The return value must be checked; if non-zero, the plaintext in m must not be used (per warn_unused_result and libsodium pattern).

functions.name: crypto_secretbox_xsalsa20poly1305_keybytes
functions.description: Returns the size in bytes of a crypto_secretbox_xsalsa20poly1305 secret key (constant 32). Use to size buffers and validate key lengths.

functions.name: crypto_secretbox_xsalsa20poly1305_noncebytes
functions.description: Returns the size in bytes of a crypto_secretbox_xsalsa20poly1305 nonce (constant 24). Use to size buffers and validate nonce lengths.

functions.name: crypto_secretbox_xsalsa20poly1305_macbytes
functions.description: Returns the size in bytes of the authentication tag (MAC) produced by crypto_secretbox_xsalsa20poly1305 (constant 16).

functions.name: crypto_secretbox_xsalsa20poly1305_messagebytes_max
functions.description: Returns the maximum allowed plaintext message size (in bytes) for the libsodium secretbox API variant without NaCl padding. Computed as crypto_stream_xsalsa20_MESSAGEBYTES_MAX - crypto_secretbox_xsalsa20poly1305_MACBYTES.

functions.name: crypto_secretbox_xsalsa20poly1305_keygen
functions.description: Fills the provided buffer with a freshly generated random key suitable for crypto_secretbox_xsalsa20poly1305. Intended for generating a new secret key using libsodium’s RNG.
requirements: k must be non-null (nonnull attribute) and point to a writable buffer of exactly crypto_secretbox_xsalsa20poly1305_KEYBYTES bytes (32).
The buffer must remain valid for the duration of the call.

functions.name: crypto_secretbox_xsalsa20poly1305_boxzerobytes
functions.description: Returns the number of leading zero bytes required in the ciphertext buffer for the NaCl-compatible, deprecated secretbox interface (constant 16).

functions.name: crypto_secretbox_xsalsa20poly1305_zerobytes
functions.description: Returns the number of leading zero bytes required in the message (plaintext) buffer for the NaCl-compatible, deprecated secretbox interface. Defined as BOXZEROBYTES + MACBYTES (16 + 16 = 32).

functions.name: crypto_secretbox_xsalsa20poly1305
functions.signature: int crypto_secretbox_xsalsa20poly1305(unsigned char *c, const unsigned char *m, unsigned long long mlen, const unsigned char *n, const unsigned char *k);
functions.description: NaCl-compatible, deprecated authenticated encryption using XSalsa20-Poly1305. Encrypts and authenticates the message m into c using nonce n and key k. This interface requires NaCl-style padding: the first crypto_secretbox_xsalsa20poly1305_ZEROBYTES bytes of m must be zero, and the first crypto_secretbox_xsalsa20poly1305_BOXZEROBYTES bytes of the resulting c will be zero.
requirements: This interface is deprecated (attribute deprecated); prefer the non-padded libsodium secretbox APIs for new code.
c, n, and k must be non-null (nonnull(1,4,5)).
m must point to a buffer of at least mlen bytes; the first crypto_secretbox_xsalsa20poly1305_ZEROBYTES bytes of m must be set to zero.
mlen must be at least crypto_secretbox_xsalsa20poly1305_ZEROBYTES; the effective plaintext length is mlen - crypto_secretbox_xsalsa20poly1305_ZEROBYTES.
c must point to a writable buffer of at least mlen bytes; the first crypto_secretbox_xsalsa20poly1305_BOXZEROBYTES bytes of c will be set to zero by convention of this interface.
n must point to a buffer of exactly crypto_secretbox_xsalsa20poly1305_NONCEBYTES bytes (24).
k must point to a buffer of exactly crypto_secretbox_xsalsa20poly1305_KEYBYTES bytes (32).
The effective plaintext length (mlen - ZEROBYTES) should not exceed crypto_secretbox_xsalsa20poly1305_messagebytes_max().

functions.name: crypto_secretbox_xsalsa20poly1305_open
functions.signature: int crypto_secretbox_xsalsa20poly1305_open(unsigned char *m, const unsigned char *c, unsigned long long clen, const unsigned char *n, const unsigned char *k);
functions.description: NaCl-compatible, deprecated decryption and verification for XSalsa20-Poly1305. Verifies and decrypts ciphertext c into m using nonce n and key k, with NaCl-style padding: c must begin with crypto_secretbox_xsalsa20poly1305_BOXZEROBYTES zero bytes, and m must begin with crypto_secretbox_xsalsa20poly1305_ZEROBYTES zero bytes. The function returns an int status (warn_unused_result) indicating authentication success or failure.
requirements: This interface is deprecated (attribute deprecated); prefer the non-padded libsodium secretbox APIs for new code.
The return value must be checked (warn_unused_result). A non-zero return indicates authentication/verification failed.
c, n, and k must be non-null (nonnull(2,4,5)).
c must point to a buffer of at least clen bytes; the first crypto_secretbox_xsalsa20poly1305_BOXZEROBYTES bytes of c must be zero.
clen must be at least crypto_secretbox_xsalsa20poly1305_BOXZEROBYTES; the effective ciphertext payload length is clen - crypto_secretbox_xsalsa20poly1305_BOXZEROBYTES.
m must point to a writable buffer of at least clen bytes; the first crypto_secretbox_xsalsa20poly1305_ZEROBYTES bytes of m are part of the NaCl padding convention.
n must point to a buffer of exactly crypto_secretbox_xsalsa20poly1305_NONCEBYTES bytes (24).
k must point to a buffer of exactly crypto_secretbox_xsalsa20poly1305_KEYBYTES bytes (32).

functions.name: crypto_secretstream_xchacha20poly1305_abytes
functions.description: Returns the number of authentication/tag bytes added to each encrypted chunk in a secretstream using XChaCha20-Poly1305. Use this to size ciphertext buffers as plaintext_len + ABYTES.

functions.name: crypto_secretstream_xchacha20poly1305_headerbytes
functions.description: Returns the size in bytes of the secretstream header that must be generated by init_push and provided to init_pull. Allocate a buffer of this size for the header.

functions.name: crypto_secretstream_xchacha20poly1305_keybytes
functions.description: Returns the required size in bytes of a secretstream key. Use to allocate key buffers and to validate inputs to key-dependent functions.

functions.name: crypto_secretstream_xchacha20poly1305_messagebytes_max
functions.description: Returns the maximum supported plaintext message size for a single push/pull operation with this primitive. Use to validate inputs and prevent overflow.

functions.name: crypto_secretstream_xchacha20poly1305_tag_message
functions.description: Returns the tag value that marks a regular message chunk. Pass this tag to push when no special semantics (push/rekey/final) are required.

functions.name: crypto_secretstream_xchacha20poly1305_tag_push
functions.description: Returns the tag value that forces the start of a new segment (a push) in the stream. Use with push to delineate message boundaries.

functions.name: crypto_secretstream_xchacha20poly1305_tag_rekey
functions.description: Returns the tag value that requests an internal key rotation after processing the chunk. Pass to push to rotate keys.

functions.name: crypto_secretstream_xchacha20poly1305_tag_final
functions.description: Returns the tag value that marks the last chunk of the stream and requests a rekey. Use with the final push to indicate end-of-stream.

functions.name: crypto_secretstream_xchacha20poly1305_statebytes
functions.description: Returns the size in bytes of crypto_secretstream_xchacha20poly1305_state. Useful for dynamic allocation or zero-initialization checks.

functions.name: crypto_secretstream_xchacha20poly1305_keygen
functions.description: Fills k with a newly generated random key suitable for secretstream XChaCha20-Poly1305 operations. Intended for creating a fresh symmetric key.
requirements: k must be non-NULL (nonnull) and point to a writable buffer of size crypto_secretstream_xchacha20poly1305_KEYBYTES.
Caller must provide storage for k; the function writes exactly KEYBYTES bytes.

functions.name: crypto_secretstream_xchacha20poly1305_init_push
functions.signature: int crypto_secretstream_xchacha20poly1305_init_push(crypto_secretstream_xchacha20poly1305_state *state, unsigned char header[crypto_secretstream_xchacha20poly1305_HEADERBYTES], const unsigned char k[crypto_secretstream_xchacha20poly1305_KEYBYTES]) __attribute__ ((nonnull));
functions.description: Initializes an encryption (push) state and outputs a header that must be sent to/used by the receiver to initialize pull. Call this before the first push.
requirements: state must be non-NULL (nonnull) and point to writable storage for a crypto_secretstream_xchacha20poly1305_state.
header must be non-NULL (nonnull) and point to a writable buffer of size crypto_secretstream_xchacha20poly1305_HEADERBYTES; on success it is filled with the stream header.
k must be non-NULL (nonnull) and point to a readable buffer of size crypto_secretstream_xchacha20poly1305_KEYBYTES.
Must be called before any crypto_secretstream_xchacha20poly1305_push on the same state.
Return value is an int; non-zero indicates failure (exact codes not specified in this header).

functions.name: crypto_secretstream_xchacha20poly1305_push
functions.signature: int crypto_secretstream_xchacha20poly1305_push(crypto_secretstream_xchacha20poly1305_state *state, unsigned char *c, unsigned long long *clen_p, const unsigned char *m, unsigned long long mlen, const unsigned char *ad, unsigned long long adlen, unsigned char tag) __attribute__ ((nonnull(1)));
functions.description: Encrypts and authenticates a message chunk m (with optional associated data ad) and appends authentication data; writes ciphertext to c and the resulting length to clen_p if provided. Use after a successful init_push, and supply a tag indicating chunk semantics.
requirements: state must be non-NULL (nonnull(1)) and must have been initialized by crypto_secretstream_xchacha20poly1305_init_push.
If c is non-NULL, it must point to a writable buffer with capacity at least mlen + crypto_secretstream_xchacha20poly1305_abytes().
If clen_p is non-NULL, it must point to writable storage for an unsigned long long to receive the ciphertext length.
m may be NULL only if mlen is 0; otherwise it must point to readable memory of size mlen.
ad may be NULL only if adlen is 0; otherwise it must point to readable memory of size adlen.
mlen should not exceed crypto_secretstream_xchacha20poly1305_messagebytes_max().
tag must be one of the tag constants returned by crypto_secretstream_xchacha20poly1305_tag_message/push/rekey/final.
Return value is an int; non-zero indicates failure (exact codes not specified in this header).

functions.name: crypto_secretstream_xchacha20poly1305_init_pull
functions.signature: int crypto_secretstream_xchacha20poly1305_init_pull(crypto_secretstream_xchacha20poly1305_state *state, const unsigned char header[crypto_secretstream_xchacha20poly1305_HEADERBYTES], const unsigned char k[crypto_secretstream_xchacha20poly1305_KEYBYTES]) __attribute__ ((nonnull));
functions.description: Initializes a decryption (pull) state from a received header and a shared key. Call this before the first pull to begin decrypting a stream.
requirements: state must be non-NULL (nonnull) and point to writable storage for a crypto_secretstream_xchacha20poly1305_state.
header must be non-NULL (nonnull) and point to a readable buffer of size crypto_secretstream_xchacha20poly1305_HEADERBYTES produced by init_push.
k must be non-NULL (nonnull) and point to a readable buffer of size crypto_secretstream_xchacha20poly1305_KEYBYTES.
Must be called before any crypto_secretstream_xchacha20poly1305_pull on the same state.
Return value is an int; non-zero indicates failure (exact codes not specified in this header).

functions.name: crypto_secretstream_xchacha20poly1305_pull
functions.signature: int crypto_secretstream_xchacha20poly1305_pull(crypto_secretstream_xchacha20poly1305_state *state, unsigned char *m, unsigned long long *mlen_p, unsigned char *tag_p, const unsigned char *c, unsigned long long clen, const unsigned char *ad, unsigned long long adlen) __attribute__ ((nonnull(1)));
functions.description: Decrypts and verifies a ciphertext chunk c (with optional associated data ad); on success writes the plaintext to m, its length to mlen_p if provided, and the chunk tag to tag_p if provided. Use after a successful init_pull for each received chunk.
requirements: state must be non-NULL (nonnull(1)) and must have been initialized by crypto_secretstream_xchacha20poly1305_init_pull.
clen must be at least crypto_secretstream_xchacha20poly1305_abytes(); otherwise decryption cannot succeed.
If m is non-NULL, it must point to a writable buffer with capacity at least (clen - crypto_secretstream_xchacha20poly1305_abytes()).
If mlen_p is non-NULL, it must point to writable storage for an unsigned long long to receive the plaintext length.
If tag_p is non-NULL, it must point to writable storage for one byte to receive the chunk tag.
c must point to readable memory of size clen.
ad may be NULL only if adlen is 0; otherwise it must point to readable memory of size adlen.
Return value is an int; non-zero indicates failure/authentication error (exact codes not specified in this header).

functions.name: crypto_secretstream_xchacha20poly1305_rekey
functions.description: Forces an explicit key rotation on an existing secretstream state. Can be used on either push or pull states to limit key reuse independently of tags.
requirements: state must point to a valid, initialized crypto_secretstream_xchacha20poly1305_state (from init_push or init_pull).
state must be writable as it will be updated in place.

functions.name: crypto_shorthash_bytes
functions.description: Returns the number of bytes in a crypto_shorthash output. Use this to size the output buffer passed to crypto_shorthash.
requirements: No arguments; can be called at any time.
The returned value should be used to allocate at least this many bytes for the output of crypto_shorthash.

functions.name: crypto_shorthash_keybytes
functions.description: Returns the number of bytes required for a crypto_shorthash key. Use this to size the key buffer for crypto_shorthash and crypto_shorthash_keygen.
requirements: No arguments; can be called at any time.
The returned value should be used to allocate the key buffer passed to crypto_shorthash and crypto_shorthash_keygen.

functions.name: crypto_shorthash_primitive
functions.description: Returns the name of the underlying short-hash primitive. In this header it is defined as "siphash24". The returned pointer refers to a read-only, null-terminated string.
requirements: The returned string must be treated as read-only.
The pointer remains valid for the lifetime of the process (typical for library string constants; exact lifetime not specified in header).

functions.name: crypto_shorthash
functions.signature: int crypto_shorthash(unsigned char *out, const unsigned char *in, unsigned long long inlen, const unsigned char *k) __attribute__ ((nonnull(1, 4)));
functions.description: Computes a fixed-size short hash (SipHash-2-4) of the input message using the provided secret key and writes the result to out. Intended for hash-table style keys or message authentication where collision resistance and keyed hashing are needed but full cryptographic hash outputs are unnecessary. Return value semantics are not specified in this header (typical libsodium functions return 0 on success).
requirements: out must be a non-null pointer (per nonnull attribute) to a writable buffer of at least crypto_shorthash_bytes() bytes.
k must be a non-null pointer (per nonnull attribute) to a readable buffer of exactly crypto_shorthash_keybytes() bytes.
in may be NULL only if inlen == 0 (safe/typical usage pattern; not enforced by attributes).
inlen may be any value representable by unsigned long long, including 0.
The output buffer must not overlap with the key buffer; other aliasing is unspecified.
The caller should check the return value according to the library’s documentation; exact success/failure conventions are not stated in this header.

functions.name: crypto_shorthash_keygen
functions.description: Fills k with a newly generated random key suitable for use with crypto_shorthash. Intended to simplify creation of a correctly sized, unpredictable key.
requirements: k must be a non-null pointer (per nonnull attribute) to a writable buffer of at least crypto_shorthash_keybytes() bytes.
The buffer k must be valid for writing the entire required key size; no overlap with read-only memory.
Library pattern inference: functions that generate random data typically require sodium_init() to be called once before first use (not stated in this header; verify against library docs).

functions.name: crypto_shorthash_siphash24_bytes
functions.description: Returns the size in bytes of the SipHash-2-4 shorthash output (64-bit). Typically used to size the output buffer for crypto_shorthash_siphash24.
requirements: No arguments; can be called at any time.
Return value is the required output size in bytes (expected 8).

functions.name: crypto_shorthash_siphash24_keybytes
functions.description: Returns the size in bytes of the SipHash-2-4 key (128-bit). Typically used to size/validate the key buffer for crypto_shorthash_siphash24.
requirements: No arguments; can be called at any time.
Return value is the required key size in bytes (expected 16).

functions.name: crypto_shorthash_siphash24
functions.signature: int crypto_shorthash_siphash24(unsigned char *out, const unsigned char *in, unsigned long long inlen, const unsigned char *k) __attribute__ ((nonnull(1, 4)));
functions.description: Computes a SipHash-2-4 shorthash (64-bit) of the message in using the 16-byte key k and writes the result to out. Intended for fast keyed hashing of short messages (e.g., hash table keys), not for general-purpose cryptographic MACs. Returns an int status (libsodium pattern: 0 on success).
requirements: out must be non-NULL and point to a writable buffer of at least crypto_shorthash_siphash24_BYTES (8) bytes (enforced by nonnull attribute).
k must be non-NULL and point to a buffer of at least crypto_shorthash_siphash24_KEYBYTES (16) bytes (enforced by nonnull attribute).
in may be NULL only if inlen is 0 (inferred from the absence of nonnull on parameter 2).
inlen is the length of the input in bytes; it must correctly describe the accessible memory region starting at in when in is non-NULL.
Caller should check the return value; nonzero indicates failure (conventional libsodium behavior).
Thread-safety and buffer aliasing between out and in are not documented here; avoid overlapping out with input/key buffers unless library documentation explicitly permits it.

functions.name: crypto_shorthash_siphashx24_bytes
functions.description: Returns the size in bytes of the SipHash-x-2-4 shorthash output (128-bit variant). Typically used to size the output buffer for crypto_shorthash_siphashx24. This API is unavailable when SODIUM_LIBRARY_MINIMAL is defined at build time.
requirements: No arguments; can be called at any time.
Availability is conditional: not available if compiled with SODIUM_LIBRARY_MINIMAL defined.
Return value is the required output size in bytes (expected 16).

functions.name: crypto_shorthash_siphashx24_keybytes
functions.description: Returns the size in bytes of the key for the SipHash-x-2-4 (128-bit output) variant. Typically used to size/validate the key buffer for crypto_shorthash_siphashx24. This API is unavailable when SODIUM_LIBRARY_MINIMAL is defined at build time.
requirements: No arguments; can be called at any time.
Availability is conditional: not available if compiled with SODIUM_LIBRARY_MINIMAL defined.
Return value is the required key size in bytes (expected 16).

functions.name: crypto_shorthash_siphashx24
functions.signature: int crypto_shorthash_siphashx24(unsigned char *out, const unsigned char *in, unsigned long long inlen, const unsigned char *k) __attribute__ ((nonnull(1, 4)));
functions.description: Computes a SipHash-x-2-4 shorthash (128-bit output) of the message in using the 16-byte key k and writes the result to out. Intended for keyed hashing of short messages with a wider (128-bit) output than SipHash-2-4. Returns an int status (libsodium pattern: 0 on success). This API is unavailable when SODIUM_LIBRARY_MINIMAL is defined at build time.
requirements: Availability is conditional: not available if compiled with SODIUM_LIBRARY_MINIMAL defined.
out must be non-NULL and point to a writable buffer of at least crypto_shorthash_siphashx24_BYTES (16) bytes (enforced by nonnull attribute).
k must be non-NULL and point to a buffer of at least crypto_shorthash_siphashx24_KEYBYTES (16) bytes (enforced by nonnull attribute).
in may be NULL only if inlen is 0 (inferred from the absence of nonnull on parameter 2).
inlen is the length of the input in bytes; it must correctly describe the accessible memory region starting at in when in is non-NULL.
Caller should check the return value; nonzero indicates failure (conventional libsodium behavior).
Thread-safety and buffer aliasing between out and in are not documented here; avoid overlapping out with input/key buffers unless library documentation explicitly permits it.

functions.name: crypto_sign_statebytes
functions.description: Returns the number of bytes required to hold a crypto_sign_state object for the streaming (pre-hash) Ed25519 signing API. Use this to allocate a state buffer when not using a stack-allocated crypto_sign_state.
requirements: No arguments.
Use the returned size to allocate a writable buffer for crypto_sign_state if allocating dynamically.
The allocated state memory must be at least crypto_sign_statebytes() bytes and properly aligned for crypto_sign_state.

functions.name: crypto_sign_bytes
functions.description: Returns the size in bytes of an Ed25519 signature (crypto_sign_BYTES). This is the length of the signature for detached signatures and the overhead added to a message in the attached-signature API.
requirements: No arguments.
Use this value to size signature buffers (detached) or to size the signed-message buffer (mlen + crypto_sign_bytes()).

functions.name: crypto_sign_seedbytes
functions.description: Returns the size in bytes of the seed required by crypto_sign_seed_keypair (crypto_sign_SEEDBYTES).
requirements: No arguments.
Seeds provided to crypto_sign_seed_keypair must be exactly crypto_sign_seedbytes() bytes.

functions.name: crypto_sign_publickeybytes
functions.description: Returns the size in bytes of an Ed25519 public key (crypto_sign_PUBLICKEYBYTES).
requirements: No arguments.
Public key buffers used with keypair or verification functions must be at least crypto_sign_publickeybytes() bytes.

functions.name: crypto_sign_secretkeybytes
functions.description: Returns the size in bytes of an Ed25519 secret key (crypto_sign_SECRETKEYBYTES).
requirements: No arguments.
Secret key buffers used with keypair or signing functions must be at least crypto_sign_secretkeybytes() bytes.

functions.name: crypto_sign_messagebytes_max
functions.description: Returns the maximum message size supported by the signing API (crypto_sign_MESSAGEBYTES_MAX).
requirements: No arguments.
Message lengths (mlen) passed to signing functions must not exceed crypto_sign_messagebytes_max().

functions.name: crypto_sign_primitive
functions.description: Returns a constant string naming the underlying signature primitive. For this header, it is "ed25519".
requirements: No arguments.
Callers must treat the returned pointer as read-only and not free it.

functions.name: crypto_sign_seed_keypair
functions.signature: int crypto_sign_seed_keypair(unsigned char *pk, unsigned char *sk, const unsigned char *seed) __attribute__ ((nonnull));
functions.description: Deterministically generates an Ed25519 key pair from a caller-provided seed. Writes the public key to pk and the secret key to sk using the Ed25519 scheme.
requirements: Thread-safety: this function is always thread-safe (per file-level comment).
pk must be a non-NULL pointer to a writable buffer of at least crypto_sign_publickeybytes() bytes.
sk must be a non-NULL pointer to a writable buffer of at least crypto_sign_secretkeybytes() bytes.
seed must be a non-NULL pointer to a readable buffer of exactly crypto_sign_seedbytes() bytes.
Return value convention is not stated in this header; typically 0 indicates success and non-zero indicates failure (inferred from libsodium conventions).

functions.name: crypto_sign_keypair
functions.description: Generates a random Ed25519 key pair. Writes the public key to pk and the secret key to sk.
requirements: Thread-safety: crypto_sign_keypair() is thread-safe provided that sodium_init() was called before; callers must call sodium_init() successfully at process start or before first use.
pk must be a non-NULL pointer to a writable buffer of at least crypto_sign_publickeybytes() bytes.
sk must be a non-NULL pointer to a writable buffer of at least crypto_sign_secretkeybytes() bytes.
Return value convention is not stated in this header; typically 0 indicates success and non-zero indicates failure (inferred from libsodium conventions).

functions.name: crypto_sign
functions.signature: int crypto_sign(unsigned char *sm, unsigned long long *smlen_p, const unsigned char *m, unsigned long long mlen, const unsigned char *sk) __attribute__ ((nonnull(1, 5)));
functions.description: Creates an attached Ed25519 signature for message m using secret key sk and outputs the signed message (signature prepended) to sm. Writes the signed message length to smlen_p if provided.
requirements: sm must be a non-NULL pointer to a writable buffer of at least mlen + crypto_sign_bytes() bytes.
smlen_p may be NULL or non-NULL; if non-NULL it must point to writable memory for the resulting length (unsigned long long).
m must point to a readable buffer of mlen bytes. m may be empty when mlen == 0.
mlen must be <= crypto_sign_messagebytes_max().
sk must be a non-NULL pointer to a readable buffer of at least crypto_sign_secretkeybytes() bytes.
Return value convention is not stated in this header; typically 0 indicates success and non-zero indicates failure (inferred).

functions.name: crypto_sign_open
functions.signature: int crypto_sign_open(unsigned char *m, unsigned long long *mlen_p, const unsigned char *sm, unsigned long long smlen, const unsigned char *pk) __attribute__ ((warn_unused_result)) __attribute__ ((nonnull(3, 5)));
functions.description: Verifies an attached Ed25519 signature and, if valid, extracts the original message from the signed-message buffer sm into m. Writes the message length to mlen_p if provided. Returns a status that must be checked (warn_unused_result).
requirements: Callers must check the return value; the result is marked warn_unused_result.
m must point to a writable buffer large enough to hold the recovered message; a safe upper bound is smlen bytes (the message is smlen - crypto_sign_bytes()).
mlen_p may be NULL or non-NULL; if non-NULL it must point to writable memory for the resulting length (unsigned long long).
sm must be a non-NULL pointer to a readable buffer of smlen bytes.
smlen must be >= crypto_sign_bytes().
pk must be a non-NULL pointer to a readable buffer of at least crypto_sign_publickeybytes() bytes.
Return value convention is not stated; typically 0 on success (valid signature) and -1 on failure (inferred).

functions.name: crypto_sign_detached
functions.signature: int crypto_sign_detached(unsigned char *sig, unsigned long long *siglen_p, const unsigned char *m, unsigned long long mlen, const unsigned char *sk) __attribute__ ((nonnull(1, 5)));
functions.description: Computes a detached Ed25519 signature of message m using secret key sk and writes it to sig. Writes the signature length to siglen_p if provided.
requirements: sig must be a non-NULL pointer to a writable buffer of at least crypto_sign_bytes() bytes.
siglen_p may be NULL or non-NULL; if non-NULL it must point to writable memory for the resulting length (unsigned long long).
m must point to a readable buffer of mlen bytes. It may be empty when mlen == 0.
mlen must be <= crypto_sign_messagebytes_max().
sk must be a non-NULL pointer to a readable buffer of at least crypto_sign_secretkeybytes() bytes.
Return value convention is not stated; typically 0 indicates success and non-zero indicates failure (inferred).

functions.name: crypto_sign_verify_detached
functions.signature: int crypto_sign_verify_detached(const unsigned char *sig, const unsigned char *m, unsigned long long mlen, const unsigned char *pk) __attribute__ ((warn_unused_result)) __attribute__ ((nonnull(1, 4)));
functions.description: Verifies a detached Ed25519 signature sig for message m with public key pk. Returns a status that must be checked (warn_unused_result).
requirements: Callers must check the return value; the result is marked warn_unused_result.
sig must be a non-NULL pointer to a readable buffer of exactly crypto_sign_bytes() bytes.
m must point to a readable buffer of mlen bytes. It may be empty when mlen == 0.
mlen must be <= crypto_sign_messagebytes_max().
pk must be a non-NULL pointer to a readable buffer of at least crypto_sign_publickeybytes() bytes.
Return value convention is not stated; typically 0 on success (valid signature) and -1 on failure (inferred).

functions.name: crypto_sign_init
functions.description: Initializes a crypto_sign_state for the streaming Ed25519 pre-hash signing API. Must be called before update and final_{create,verify}.
requirements: state must point to a writable crypto_sign_state object, backed by at least crypto_sign_statebytes() bytes.
Call before any crypto_sign_update or crypto_sign_final_* on the same state.
A given state should not be re-used for a new message without reinitializing via crypto_sign_init.
Return value convention is not stated; typically 0 indicates success (inferred).

functions.name: crypto_sign_update
functions.signature: int crypto_sign_update(crypto_sign_state *state, const unsigned char *m, unsigned long long mlen) __attribute__ ((nonnull(1)));
functions.description: Feeds a chunk of message data into an initialized crypto_sign_state for streaming (pre-hash) Ed25519 signing or verification.
requirements: state must be a non-NULL pointer to an initialized crypto_sign_state (initialized with crypto_sign_init).
If mlen > 0, m must point to a readable buffer of at least mlen bytes.
May be called zero or more times after crypto_sign_init and before crypto_sign_final_create or crypto_sign_final_verify.
Return value convention is not stated; typically 0 indicates success (inferred).

functions.name: crypto_sign_final_create
functions.signature: int crypto_sign_final_create(crypto_sign_state *state, unsigned char *sig, unsigned long long *siglen_p, const unsigned char *sk) __attribute__ ((nonnull(1, 2, 4)));
functions.description: Finalizes the streaming signing operation and produces a detached Ed25519 signature for the message accumulated in state using secret key sk. Writes the signature to sig and its length to siglen_p if provided.
requirements: state must be a non-NULL pointer to a crypto_sign_state that has been initialized with crypto_sign_init and updated with zero or more chunks.
sig must be a non-NULL pointer to a writable buffer of at least crypto_sign_bytes() bytes.
siglen_p may be NULL or non-NULL; if non-NULL it must point to writable memory for the resulting length (unsigned long long).
sk must be a non-NULL pointer to a readable buffer of at least crypto_sign_secretkeybytes() bytes.
After finalization, the state should be reinitialized before signing a new message (inferred state-machine requirement).
Return value convention is not stated; typically 0 indicates success (inferred).

functions.name: crypto_sign_final_verify
functions.signature: int crypto_sign_final_verify(crypto_sign_state *state, const unsigned char *sig, const unsigned char *pk) __attribute__ ((warn_unused_result)) __attribute__ ((nonnull));
functions.description: Finalizes the streaming verification operation by checking that sig matches the message accumulated in state using public key pk. Returns a status that must be checked (warn_unused_result).
requirements: Callers must check the return value; the result is marked warn_unused_result.
state must be a non-NULL pointer to a crypto_sign_state that has been initialized with crypto_sign_init and updated with zero or more chunks corresponding to the signed message.
sig must be a non-NULL pointer to a readable buffer of exactly crypto_sign_bytes() bytes.
pk must be a non-NULL pointer to a readable buffer of at least crypto_sign_publickeybytes() bytes.
After finalization, the state should be reinitialized before verifying a new message (inferred state-machine requirement).
Return value convention is not stated; typically 0 on success (valid signature) and -1 on failure (inferred).

functions.name: crypto_sign_ed25519ph_statebytes
functions.description: Returns the size in bytes of the crypto_sign_ed25519ph_state structure used for Ed25519ph (pre-hash) streaming signing. Use to allocate a state buffer if needed.

functions.name: crypto_sign_ed25519_bytes
functions.description: Returns the length in bytes of an Ed25519 signature (crypto_sign_ed25519_BYTES == 64). Useful for sizing buffers for detached signatures or for the signature portion of combined signed messages.

functions.name: crypto_sign_ed25519_seedbytes
functions.description: Returns the length in bytes of an Ed25519 seed (crypto_sign_ed25519_SEEDBYTES == 32).

functions.name: crypto_sign_ed25519_publickeybytes
functions.description: Returns the length in bytes of an Ed25519 public key (crypto_sign_ed25519_PUBLICKEYBYTES == 32).

functions.name: crypto_sign_ed25519_secretkeybytes
functions.description: Returns the length in bytes of an Ed25519 secret key (crypto_sign_ed25519_SECRETKEYBYTES == 64).

functions.name: crypto_sign_ed25519_messagebytes_max
functions.description: Returns the maximum message length (in bytes) that can be signed using Ed25519 (SODIUM_SIZE_MAX - crypto_sign_ed25519_BYTES). Use to validate inputs before signing.

functions.name: crypto_sign_ed25519
functions.signature: int crypto_sign_ed25519(unsigned char *sm, unsigned long long *smlen_p, const unsigned char *m, unsigned long long mlen, const unsigned char *sk);
functions.description: Signs a message m (mlen bytes) with an Ed25519 secret key sk, producing a signed message sm that contains the signature followed by the message. On success, writes the signed message length to smlen_p and returns 0; on failure, returns non-zero.
requirements: sm must be a valid, writable buffer large enough for mlen + crypto_sign_ed25519_BYTES bytes.
smlen_p must be a valid, writable pointer to hold the resulting signed message length.
m must point to a buffer of at least mlen bytes (mlen may be 0).
sk must be a valid pointer to an Ed25519 secret key of length crypto_sign_ed25519_SECRETKEYBYTES bytes.
mlen should not exceed crypto_sign_ed25519_messagebytes_max().
sm, m, and sk pointers must be non-NULL (per nonnull(1,5) attribute).

functions.name: crypto_sign_ed25519_open
functions.signature: int crypto_sign_ed25519_open(unsigned char *m, unsigned long long *mlen_p, const unsigned char *sm, unsigned long long smlen, const unsigned char *pk);
functions.description: Verifies a signed message sm (smlen bytes) using an Ed25519 public key pk and, if valid, outputs the original message into m and its length into mlen_p. Returns 0 on successful verification; non-zero on failure. The return value should be checked by the caller.
requirements: m must be a valid, writable buffer large enough to hold the recovered message (up to smlen - crypto_sign_ed25519_BYTES bytes).
mlen_p must be a valid, writable pointer to receive the message length.
sm must point to a buffer of length smlen bytes; smlen should be at least crypto_sign_ed25519_BYTES.
pk must point to an Ed25519 public key of length crypto_sign_ed25519_PUBLICKEYBYTES bytes.
sm and pk must be non-NULL (per nonnull(3,5) attribute).
The function is annotated warn_unused_result; callers should check the return value and must not use output if verification fails.

functions.name: crypto_sign_ed25519_detached
functions.signature: int crypto_sign_ed25519_detached(unsigned char *sig, unsigned long long *siglen_p, const unsigned char *m, unsigned long long mlen, const unsigned char *sk);
functions.description: Computes a detached Ed25519 signature of message m (mlen bytes) using secret key sk. Writes the signature to sig and its length to siglen_p. Returns 0 on success, non-zero on failure.
requirements: sig must be a valid, writable buffer of at least crypto_sign_ed25519_BYTES bytes.
siglen_p must be a valid, writable pointer to receive the signature length.
m must point to a buffer of at least mlen bytes (mlen may be 0).
sk must be a valid pointer to an Ed25519 secret key of length crypto_sign_ed25519_SECRETKEYBYTES bytes.
mlen should not exceed crypto_sign_ed25519_messagebytes_max().
sig and sk must be non-NULL (per nonnull(1,5) attribute).

functions.name: crypto_sign_ed25519_verify_detached
functions.signature: int crypto_sign_ed25519_verify_detached(const unsigned char *sig, const unsigned char *m, unsigned long long mlen, const unsigned char *pk);
functions.description: Verifies a detached Ed25519 signature sig for message m (mlen bytes) using public key pk. Returns 0 on successful verification; non-zero otherwise. The return value should be checked by the caller.
requirements: sig must point to a buffer of length crypto_sign_ed25519_BYTES bytes.
m must point to a buffer of at least mlen bytes (mlen may be 0).
pk must point to an Ed25519 public key of length crypto_sign_ed25519_PUBLICKEYBYTES bytes.
sig and pk must be non-NULL (per nonnull(1,4) attribute).
The function is annotated warn_unused_result; callers should check the return value and must not accept the signature if verification fails.

functions.name: crypto_sign_ed25519_keypair
functions.description: Generates a new random Ed25519 key pair. Writes the public key to pk and the secret key to sk. Returns 0 on success, non-zero on failure.
requirements: pk must be a valid, writable buffer of at least crypto_sign_ed25519_PUBLICKEYBYTES bytes.
sk must be a valid, writable buffer of at least crypto_sign_ed25519_SECRETKEYBYTES bytes.
pk and sk must be non-NULL (per nonnull attribute).

functions.name: crypto_sign_ed25519_seed_keypair
functions.signature: int crypto_sign_ed25519_seed_keypair(unsigned char *pk, unsigned char *sk, const unsigned char *seed);
functions.description: Derives an Ed25519 key pair from a provided seed. Writes the public key to pk and the secret key to sk. Returns 0 on success, non-zero on failure.
requirements: pk must be a valid, writable buffer of at least crypto_sign_ed25519_PUBLICKEYBYTES bytes.
sk must be a valid, writable buffer of at least crypto_sign_ed25519_SECRETKEYBYTES bytes.
seed must point to a buffer of length crypto_sign_ed25519_SEEDBYTES bytes.
All parameters must be non-NULL (per nonnull attribute).

functions.name: crypto_sign_ed25519_pk_to_curve25519
functions.description: Converts an Ed25519 public key to the corresponding Curve25519 (X25519) public key. Returns 0 on success; non-zero on failure. The return value should be checked by the caller.
requirements: curve25519_pk must be a valid, writable buffer of 32 bytes.
ed25519_pk must point to a buffer of length crypto_sign_ed25519_PUBLICKEYBYTES bytes.
Both parameters must be non-NULL (per nonnull attribute).
The function is annotated warn_unused_result; callers should check the return value.

functions.name: crypto_sign_ed25519_sk_to_curve25519
functions.description: Converts an Ed25519 secret key to the corresponding Curve25519 (X25519) secret key. Returns 0 on success; non-zero on failure.
requirements: curve25519_sk must be a valid, writable buffer of 32 bytes.
ed25519_sk must point to a buffer of length crypto_sign_ed25519_SECRETKEYBYTES bytes.
Both parameters must be non-NULL (per nonnull attribute).

functions.name: crypto_sign_ed25519_sk_to_seed
functions.signature: int crypto_sign_ed25519_sk_to_seed(unsigned char *seed, const unsigned char *sk);
functions.description: Extracts the seed from an Ed25519 secret key sk and writes it to seed. Returns 0 on success; non-zero on failure.
requirements: seed must be a valid, writable buffer of length crypto_sign_ed25519_SEEDBYTES bytes.
sk must point to a buffer of length crypto_sign_ed25519_SECRETKEYBYTES bytes.
Both parameters must be non-NULL (per nonnull attribute).

functions.name: crypto_sign_ed25519_sk_to_pk
functions.signature: int crypto_sign_ed25519_sk_to_pk(unsigned char *pk, const unsigned char *sk);
functions.description: Derives the public key pk from an Ed25519 secret key sk. Returns 0 on success; non-zero on failure.
requirements: pk must be a valid, writable buffer of length crypto_sign_ed25519_PUBLICKEYBYTES bytes.
sk must point to a buffer of length crypto_sign_ed25519_SECRETKEYBYTES bytes.
Both parameters must be non-NULL (per nonnull attribute).

functions.name: crypto_sign_ed25519ph_init
functions.description: Initializes a streaming Ed25519ph (pre-hash) signing state. Call before update/final functions. Returns 0 on success; non-zero on failure.
requirements: state must be a valid, writable pointer (per nonnull attribute).
Must be called before crypto_sign_ed25519ph_update and crypto_sign_ed25519ph_final_* on the same state.

functions.name: crypto_sign_ed25519ph_update
functions.signature: int crypto_sign_ed25519ph_update(crypto_sign_ed25519ph_state *state, const unsigned char *m, unsigned long long mlen);
functions.description: Feeds a message chunk m (mlen bytes) into the Ed25519ph streaming pre-hash state. Can be called multiple times after init. Returns 0 on success; non-zero on failure.
requirements: state must be a valid, initialized pointer from crypto_sign_ed25519ph_init (per nonnull(1) attribute).
m must point to at least mlen bytes if mlen > 0 (pointer may be NULL if mlen == 0 is intended; not explicitly stated).

functions.name: crypto_sign_ed25519ph_final_create
functions.signature: int crypto_sign_ed25519ph_final_create(crypto_sign_ed25519ph_state *state, unsigned char *sig, unsigned long long *siglen_p, const unsigned char *sk);
functions.description: Finalizes the Ed25519ph pre-hash and creates a detached signature using secret key sk. Writes the signature to sig and optionally its length to siglen_p. Returns 0 on success; non-zero on failure.
requirements: state must be a valid, initialized pointer from crypto_sign_ed25519ph_init (per nonnull(1) attribute).
sig must be a valid, writable buffer of at least crypto_sign_ed25519_BYTES bytes (per nonnull(2) attribute).
sk must point to an Ed25519 secret key of length crypto_sign_ed25519_SECRETKEYBYTES bytes (per nonnull(4) attribute).
If provided, siglen_p must be a valid, writable pointer.

functions.name: crypto_sign_ed25519ph_final_verify
functions.signature: int crypto_sign_ed25519ph_final_verify(crypto_sign_ed25519ph_state *state, const unsigned char *sig, const unsigned char *pk);
functions.description: Finalizes the Ed25519ph pre-hash and verifies the detached signature sig with public key pk. Returns 0 on successful verification; non-zero otherwise. The return value should be checked by the caller.
requirements: state, sig, and pk must be non-NULL (per nonnull attribute).
state must have been initialized with crypto_sign_ed25519ph_init and updated with the message to be verified.
sig must point to a buffer of length crypto_sign_ed25519_BYTES bytes.
pk must point to a buffer of length crypto_sign_ed25519_PUBLICKEYBYTES bytes.
The function is annotated warn_unused_result; callers should check the return value and must not accept the signature if verification fails.

functions.name: crypto_stream_keybytes
functions.description: Returns the required key size (in bytes) for the crypto_stream* APIs. Use this to allocate or validate key buffers. Notes: This stream cipher is not authenticated; use crypto_box* for AEAD use cases.

functions.name: crypto_stream_noncebytes
functions.description: Returns the required nonce size (in bytes) for the crypto_stream* APIs. Use this to allocate or validate nonce buffers.

functions.name: crypto_stream_messagebytes_max
functions.description: Returns the maximum supported message length (in bytes) for crypto_stream* operations. Use this to validate input lengths before encryption/decryption.

functions.name: crypto_stream_primitive
functions.description: Returns the name of the underlying stream cipher primitive ("xsalsa20" in this build). The returned pointer refers to a static, immutable string.
requirements: Caller must not attempt to modify or free the returned string pointer.

functions.name: crypto_stream
functions.signature: SODIUM_EXPORT int crypto_stream(unsigned char *c, unsigned long long clen, const unsigned char *n, const unsigned char *k) __attribute__ ((nonnull));
functions.description: Generates a keystream of length clen bytes using the xsalsa20 primitive and writes it to c. Typical usage: generate keystream and XOR with plaintext/ciphertext externally, or use crypto_stream_xor to do this in one step. Returns 0 on success (per libsodium conventions). Security note: this is a stream cipher, not authenticated encryption.
requirements: c, n, and k must be non-null pointers (nonnull attribute applies to all pointer parameters).
c must reference a writable buffer of at least clen bytes.
n must reference a buffer of exactly crypto_stream_NONCEBYTES bytes.
k must reference a buffer of exactly crypto_stream_KEYBYTES bytes.
clen should be less than or equal to crypto_stream_MESSAGEBYTES_MAX (use crypto_stream_messagebytes_max() to query).
For security, the (key, nonce) pair must never be reused across different messages.

functions.name: crypto_stream_xor
functions.signature: SODIUM_EXPORT int crypto_stream_xor(unsigned char *c, const unsigned char *m, unsigned long long mlen, const unsigned char *n, const unsigned char *k) __attribute__ ((nonnull(1, 4, 5)));
functions.description: XORs the xsalsa20 keystream with m (mlen bytes) and writes the result to c (encrypts or decrypts, since XOR is its own inverse). Returns 0 on success (per libsodium conventions). Security note: this is not authenticated encryption; use crypto_box* if you need integrity/authentication.
requirements: c, n, and k must be non-null pointers (as per nonnull(1,4,5) attribute).
c must reference a writable buffer of at least mlen bytes.
If m is non-null, it must reference a readable buffer of at least mlen bytes.
If m is null, mlen must be 0 (implied by nonnull attribute excluding parameter 2).
n must reference a buffer of exactly crypto_stream_NONCEBYTES bytes.
k must reference a buffer of exactly crypto_stream_KEYBYTES bytes.
mlen should be less than or equal to crypto_stream_MESSAGEBYTES_MAX (use crypto_stream_messagebytes_max() to query).
For security, the (key, nonce) pair must never be reused across different messages.
Caller should check the return value and handle non-zero as an error.

functions.name: crypto_stream_keygen
functions.description: Fills k with a newly generated random key suitable for use with crypto_stream/crypto_stream_xor. Intended as the standard way to obtain a correctly-sized, high-entropy key for this API.
requirements: k must be a non-null pointer to a writable buffer of at least crypto_stream_KEYBYTES bytes.
The generated key should be kept secret and used with nonces that are never reused for the same key.

functions.name: crypto_stream_chacha20_keybytes
functions.description: Returns the size in bytes of a ChaCha20 key (classic variant). Use this to size key buffers. Typical libsodium behavior is to return 32.

functions.name: crypto_stream_chacha20_noncebytes
functions.description: Returns the size in bytes of a ChaCha20 nonce (classic variant with 64-bit nonce). Use this to size nonce buffers. Typical value is 8.

functions.name: crypto_stream_chacha20_messagebytes_max
functions.description: Returns the maximum message length (in bytes) supported by the ChaCha20 classic-variant APIs on this platform. Use to validate lengths before encryption/decryption.

functions.name: crypto_stream_chacha20
functions.signature: int crypto_stream_chacha20(unsigned char *c, unsigned long long clen, const unsigned char *n, const unsigned char *k);
functions.description: Generates clen bytes of the ChaCha20 keystream (classic variant, 64-bit nonce, 64-bit counter) into c using nonce n and key k. Commonly used to create a keystream or with XOR to encrypt/decrypt. Return value semantics are not documented here; in libsodium this typically returns 0 on success.
requirements: c must be a valid, writable buffer of at least clen bytes.
n must point to a buffer of exactly crypto_stream_chacha20_NONCEBYTES (8) bytes.
k must point to a buffer of exactly crypto_stream_chacha20_KEYBYTES (32) bytes.
clen must be less than or equal to crypto_stream_chacha20_messagebytes_max().
For security, the (key, nonce) pair should not be reused (inferred from stream cipher usage).
This function provides no authentication; do not assume integrity or authenticity of any XORed data (stated in file-level warning).

functions.name: crypto_stream_chacha20_xor
functions.signature: int crypto_stream_chacha20_xor(unsigned char *c, const unsigned char *m, unsigned long long mlen, const unsigned char *n, const unsigned char *k);
functions.description: Encrypts or decrypts mlen bytes by XORing message m with the ChaCha20 keystream derived from nonce n and key k, writing the result to c. Classic variant (64-bit nonce, 64-bit counter). Can be used for in-place operation in libsodium. Return value semantics are not documented here; typically returns 0 on success.
requirements: c must be a valid, writable buffer of at least mlen bytes.
If mlen > 0, m should point to a readable buffer of at least mlen bytes; m may be NULL only if mlen == 0 (inferred from nonnull attribute excluding m).
c and m may be the same buffer for in-place encryption/decryption (inferred from libsodium XOR API behavior).
n must point to a buffer of exactly crypto_stream_chacha20_NONCEBYTES (8) bytes.
k must point to a buffer of exactly crypto_stream_chacha20_KEYBYTES (32) bytes.
mlen must be less than or equal to crypto_stream_chacha20_messagebytes_max().
For security, do not reuse the same (key, nonce) pair for different messages (inferred from stream cipher usage).
This function provides no authentication; callers must handle integrity separately (stated in file-level warning).

functions.name: crypto_stream_chacha20_xor_ic
functions.signature: int crypto_stream_chacha20_xor_ic(unsigned char *c, const unsigned char *m, unsigned long long mlen, const unsigned char *n, uint64_t ic, const unsigned char *k);
functions.description: Like crypto_stream_chacha20_xor but starts from an explicit initial 64-bit block counter ic. Useful for random access within a stream. Classic variant (64-bit nonce). Return value semantics are not documented; typically 0 on success.
requirements: c must be a valid, writable buffer of at least mlen bytes.
If mlen > 0, m should point to a readable buffer of at least mlen bytes; m may be NULL only if mlen == 0 (inferred from nonnull attribute excluding m).
c and m may be the same buffer for in-place operation (inferred from libsodium XOR API behavior).
n must point to a buffer of exactly crypto_stream_chacha20_NONCEBYTES (8) bytes.
k must point to a buffer of exactly crypto_stream_chacha20_KEYBYTES (32) bytes.
mlen must be less than or equal to crypto_stream_chacha20_messagebytes_max().
ic is a 64-bit initial counter; any uint64_t value is allowed (no range restriction stated).
Avoid reusing the same (key, nonce, counter range) across messages (inferred from stream cipher usage).
No authentication is provided; integrity must be handled separately (stated in file-level warning).

functions.name: crypto_stream_chacha20_keygen
functions.description: Fills k with a newly generated random ChaCha20 key for the classic variant. Use this to create a secure key of the correct size.
requirements: k must be a valid, writable buffer of at least crypto_stream_chacha20_KEYBYTES (32) bytes.
The output key must be kept secret and used with nonces of size crypto_stream_chacha20_NONCEBYTES (8) bytes (usage constraint inferred).

functions.name: crypto_stream_chacha20_ietf_keybytes
functions.description: Returns the size in bytes of a ChaCha20-ietf key. Typical value is 32. Use to size key buffers.

functions.name: crypto_stream_chacha20_ietf_noncebytes
functions.description: Returns the size in bytes of a ChaCha20-ietf nonce (IETF variant with 96-bit nonce). Typical value is 12.

functions.name: crypto_stream_chacha20_ietf_messagebytes_max
functions.description: Returns the maximum message length (in bytes) supported by the ChaCha20-ietf APIs on this platform. For IETF ChaCha20 this is min(SIZE_MAX, 64 * 2^32).

functions.name: crypto_stream_chacha20_ietf
functions.signature: int crypto_stream_chacha20_ietf(unsigned char *c, unsigned long long clen, const unsigned char *n, const unsigned char *k);
functions.description: Generates clen bytes of the ChaCha20-ietf keystream (96-bit nonce, 32-bit counter) into c using nonce n and key k. Often used as a keystream generator for XOR operations. Return value semantics are not documented here; typically 0 on success.
requirements: c must be a valid, writable buffer of at least clen bytes.
n must point to a buffer of exactly crypto_stream_chacha20_ietf_NONCEBYTES (12) bytes.
k must point to a buffer of exactly crypto_stream_chacha20_ietf_KEYBYTES (32) bytes.
clen must be less than or equal to crypto_stream_chacha20_ietf_messagebytes_max().
For security, the (key, nonce) pair should not be reused (inferred from stream cipher usage).
This function provides no authentication; integrity/authenticity are not provided (stated in file-level warning).

functions.signature: void sodium_memzero(void * const pnt, const size_t len);
functions.description: Securely wipes len bytes at pnt by overwriting the memory (intended to avoid being optimized out). Use to clear sensitive data in RAM.
requirements: pnt must reference a writable region of at least len bytes.
If len is 0, behavior is effectively a no-op; otherwise pnt must be valid.
The pointed memory must remain accessible/writable for the duration of the call.

functions.name: sodium_stackzero
functions.description: Overwrites len bytes on the stack with zeros. Typically used to clear stack-allocated sensitive data before returning.
requirements: len specifies the number of stack bytes to clear; exact stack region and calling convention handling are implementation-defined (details unknown).
Should be called from the scope where the target stack memory is valid (details unknown).

functions.name: sodium_memcmp
functions.signature: int sodium_memcmp(const void * const b1_, const void * const b2_, size_t len) __attribute__ ((warn_unused_result));
functions.description: Constant-time comparison of two buffers for equality, intended for secret data (e.g., keys). Returns 0 if equal and -1 if different. Not for lexicographical ordering.
requirements: b1_ and b2_ must each point to a readable region of at least len bytes.
Callers should not ignore the return value (warn_unused_result).
Use only to test equality of secret data; do not use for sorting or ordering.
len must match the intended comparison length for both buffers.

functions.name: sodium_compare
functions.signature: int sodium_compare(const unsigned char *b1_, const unsigned char *b2_, size_t len) __attribute__ ((warn_unused_result));
functions.description: Lexicographically compares two byte arrays of length len. Returns -1 if b1_ < b2_, 1 if b1_ > b2_, and 0 if equal. Suitable for lexicographic comparisons or comparing little-endian nonces/counters; slower than sodium_memcmp() for equality checks.
requirements: b1_ and b2_ must each point to a readable region of at least len bytes.
Callers should not ignore the return value (warn_unused_result).
Use for ordering comparisons; for constant-time equality checks prefer sodium_memcmp().

functions.name: sodium_is_zero
functions.signature: int sodium_is_zero(const unsigned char *n, const size_t nlen);
functions.description: Checks whether all nlen bytes in n are zero. Returns a boolean-like int (exact return convention unspecified; typically 1 if zero, 0 otherwise, but not stated).
requirements: n must point to a readable region of at least nlen bytes.
The exact return value convention is not documented here; callers should treat nonzero/zero as success/failure accordingly (details unknown).

functions.name: sodium_increment
functions.signature: void sodium_increment(unsigned char *n, const size_t nlen);
functions.description: Interprets n as a little-endian unsigned integer and increments it in place over nlen bytes (wraps on overflow). Useful for incrementing nonces/counters.
requirements: n must point to a writable region of at least nlen bytes.
The buffer content is treated as a little-endian integer; ensure this matches protocol expectations.
If n overflows, it wraps modulo 2^(8*nlen).

functions.name: sodium_add
functions.signature: void sodium_add(unsigned char *a, const unsigned char *b, const size_t len);
functions.description: Computes a = (a + b) modulo 2^(8*len) treating both a and b as little-endian integers of len bytes. Operates in place on a.
requirements: a must point to a writable region of at least len bytes.
b must point to a readable region of at least len bytes.
Operation is modulo 2^(8*len) with little-endian interpretation.

functions.name: sodium_sub
functions.signature: void sodium_sub(unsigned char *a, const unsigned char *b, const size_t len);
functions.description: Computes a = (a − b) modulo 2^(8*len) treating both a and b as little-endian integers of len bytes. Operates in place on a.
requirements: a must point to a writable region of at least len bytes.
b must point to a readable region of at least len bytes.
Operation is modulo 2^(8*len) with little-endian interpretation.

functions.name: sodium_bin2hex
functions.signature: char *sodium_bin2hex(char * const hex, const size_t hex_maxlen, const unsigned char * const bin, const size_t bin_len) __attribute__ ((nonnull(1)));
functions.description: Encodes bin (bin_len bytes) into a lowercase hexadecimal C string written to hex, NUL-terminated. Returns hex on success.
requirements: hex must be non-NULL (nonnull(1)) and point to a writable buffer of at least hex_maxlen bytes.
hex_maxlen must be large enough to hold bin_len*2 + 1 bytes (including the trailing NUL).
bin must point to a readable region of at least bin_len bytes.
On failure behavior/return is not specified here; callers should check the return pointer (details unknown).

functions.name: sodium_hex2bin
functions.signature: int sodium_hex2bin(unsigned char * const bin, const size_t bin_maxlen, const char * const hex, const size_t hex_len, const char * const ignore, size_t * const bin_len, const char ** const hex_end) __attribute__ ((nonnull(1)));
functions.description: Decodes a hexadecimal string hex (length hex_len) into binary written to bin, optionally ignoring characters from ignore. Writes the number of bytes written to bin_len (if non-NULL) and can return a pointer to the first unparsed character via hex_end (if non-NULL). Returns an int status (exact codes not documented here).
requirements: bin must be non-NULL (nonnull(1)) and point to a writable buffer of at least bin_maxlen bytes.
hex must point to a readable buffer of at least hex_len characters; it need not be NUL-terminated if hex_len is provided.
ignore may be NULL or a C string of characters to skip in hex (exact accepted set unspecified here).
If provided, bin_len must be a valid pointer to receive the decoded length.
If provided, hex_end must be a valid pointer to receive a pointer into hex after the last parsed character.
Callers must check the returned int status; exact success/failure values are not specified here.

functions.name: sodium_base64_encoded_len
functions.signature: size_t sodium_base64_encoded_len(const size_t bin_len, const int variant);
functions.description: Computes the required buffer length to base64-encode bin_len bytes using the given variant, including space for the trailing NUL.
requirements: variant must be one of the defined sodium_base64 variants (sodium_base64_VARIANT_ORIGINAL, _ORIGINAL_NO_PADDING, _URLSAFE, _URLSAFE_NO_PADDING).
bin_len is the number of input bytes to be encoded; result includes the trailing NUL.

functions.name: sodium_bin2base64
functions.signature: char *sodium_bin2base64(char * const b64, const size_t b64_maxlen, const unsigned char * const bin, const size_t bin_len, const int variant) __attribute__ ((nonnull(1)));
functions.description: Encodes bin (bin_len bytes) into a base64 string according to variant and writes it into b64, NUL-terminated. Returns b64 on success.
requirements: b64 must be non-NULL (nonnull(1)) and point to a writable buffer of at least b64_maxlen bytes.
b64_maxlen must be large enough; use sodium_base64_encoded_len(bin_len, variant) to size the buffer (includes trailing NUL).
bin must point to a readable region of at least bin_len bytes.
variant must be one of the sodium_base64_VARIANT_* constants.
Callers should check the return value (pointer) for success/failure (exact failure conditions unspecified here).

functions.name: sodium_base642bin
functions.signature: int sodium_base642bin(unsigned char * const bin, const size_t bin_maxlen, const char * const b64, const size_t b64_len, const char * const ignore, size_t * const bin_len, const char ** const b64_end, const int variant) __attribute__ ((nonnull(1)));
functions.description: Decodes a base64 string b64 (length b64_len) according to variant into binary written to bin. Optionally ignores characters from ignore. Writes number of bytes produced to bin_len (if non-NULL) and can return a pointer to the first unparsed character via b64_end (if non-NULL). Returns int status (exact codes not documented here).
requirements: bin must be non-NULL (nonnull(1)) and point to a writable buffer of at least bin_maxlen bytes.
b64 must point to a readable buffer of at least b64_len characters; it need not be NUL-terminated if b64_len is provided.
ignore may be NULL or a C string of characters to skip (exact accepted set unspecified here).
If provided, bin_len must be a valid pointer to receive the decoded length.
If provided, b64_end must be a valid pointer to receive a pointer into b64 after the last parsed character.
variant must be one of the sodium_base64_VARIANT_* constants.
Callers must check the return value for success/failure; exact codes unspecified here.

functions.name: sodium_mlock
functions.signature: int sodium_mlock(void * const addr, const size_t len) __attribute__ ((nonnull));
functions.description: Attempts to lock len bytes starting at addr into RAM to avoid swapping sensitive data to disk. Returns an int status (platform-dependent; exact codes not documented here).
requirements: addr must be non-NULL (nonnull) and point to a valid region of at least len bytes.
The region must be accessible to the process; platform-specific limits may apply (e.g., resource limits).
Callers should check and handle the return value; success/failure codes are not specified here.

functions.name: sodium_munlock
functions.signature: int sodium_munlock(void * const addr, const size_t len) __attribute__ ((nonnull));
functions.description: Unlocks a memory region previously locked with sodium_mlock. Returns an int status (exact codes not documented here).
requirements: addr must be non-NULL (nonnull) and point to a region of at least len bytes that was previously locked.
Callers should check and handle the return value; success/failure codes are not specified here.

functions.name: sodium_malloc
functions.description: Allocates a protected memory region intended for sensitive data. The region is filled with 0xd0, is surrounded by guard pages (with canary), and may trigger a fault on overflow/underflow. Not a general-purpose allocator.
requirements: size is the requested user region size; allocation incurs additional guard pages and metadata.
The returned pointer must be freed with sodium_free (do not mix with standard free/realloc).
The returned address may not be aligned if size is not a multiple of the required alignment (per comment).
Each allocation consumes 3–4 additional pages and is significantly slower than standard allocation.
Intended for secret keys/messages; not for general-purpose allocation.
For certain packed structs (e.g., crypto_generichash_state), use the library-provided size function (e.g., crypto_generichash_statebytes()) to ensure proper alignment.

functions.name: sodium_allocarray
functions.description: Allocates a protected memory region for an array of count elements of size bytes each, with the same guard/overflow protections as sodium_malloc. Intended for sensitive data.
requirements: The returned pointer must be freed with sodium_free (do not mix with standard free/realloc).
Not a general-purpose allocator; incurs guard pages and higher overhead.
Allocated region is filled with 0xd0 and protected by guard pages and canary as described.
Behavior on multiplication overflow (count * size) is not documented here; callers should validate sizes to avoid overflow (details unknown).

functions.name: sodium_free
functions.description: Frees memory allocated by sodium_malloc or sodium_allocarray, securely handling the protected region.
requirements: ptr must be a pointer previously returned by sodium_malloc or sodium_allocarray (or NULL if allowed; NULL handling not specified here).
Do not pass pointers allocated by standard malloc/calloc/realloc.
After freeing, the pointer must not be used again (no double-free).

functions.name: sodium_mprotect_noaccess
functions.description: Changes protection of a region allocated by sodium_malloc/allocarray to no-access (no read/write). Useful to lock down secrets when not in use. Returns int status (exact codes not documented here).
requirements: ptr must be non-NULL (nonnull) and refer to a region allocated by sodium_malloc or sodium_allocarray.
Callers should check and handle the return value; exact codes unspecified.
After this call, any access to the region will fault until permissions are changed.

functions.name: sodium_mprotect_readonly
functions.description: Changes protection of a region allocated by sodium_malloc/allocarray to read-only. Returns int status (exact codes not documented here).
requirements: ptr must be non-NULL (nonnull) and refer to a region allocated by sodium_malloc or sodium_allocarray.
Callers should check and handle the return value; exact codes unspecified.
After this call, writes to the region will fault until permissions are changed.

functions.name: sodium_mprotect_readwrite
functions.description: Changes protection of a region allocated by sodium_malloc/allocarray to read/write (normal access). Returns int status (exact codes not documented here).
requirements: ptr must be non-NULL (nonnull) and refer to a region allocated by sodium_malloc or sodium_allocarray.
Callers should check and handle the return value; exact codes unspecified.
Use to re-enable read/write access after noaccess/readonly.

functions.name: sodium_pad
functions.signature: int sodium_pad(size_t *padded_buflen_p, unsigned char *buf, size_t unpadded_buflen, size_t blocksize, size_t max_buflen) __attribute__ ((nonnull(2)));
functions.description: Pads the first unpadded_buflen bytes in buf up to a multiple of blocksize, not exceeding max_buflen, and writes the resulting total length to padded_buflen_p. Padding scheme details are not documented here.
requirements: buf must be non-NULL (nonnull(2)) and point to a writable buffer with capacity of at least max_buflen bytes.
unpadded_buflen must be less than or equal to max_buflen.
blocksize determines the target block size; exact valid range and scheme are not specified here (details unknown).
padded_buflen_p, if non-NULL, must be writable to receive the new length (exact NULL allowance not stated; treat as optional based on signature).
Callers must check the return value; exact success/failure codes are not specified here.

functions.name: sodium_unpad
functions.signature: int sodium_unpad(size_t *unpadded_buflen_p, const unsigned char *buf, size_t padded_buflen, size_t blocksize) __attribute__ ((nonnull(2)));
functions.description: Removes padding from a buffer of length padded_buflen and writes the unpadded length to unpadded_buflen_p according to the padding scheme used by sodium_pad. Returns int status (exact codes not documented here).
requirements: buf must be non-NULL (nonnull(2)) and point to a readable buffer of at least padded_buflen bytes.
padded_buflen must correspond to data that was previously padded with the same blocksize; otherwise unpad will fail (exact conditions unspecified).
blocksize must match the one used for padding; valid range not specified here (details unknown).
unpadded_buflen_p must be a valid pointer to receive the result (NULL allowance not specified).
Callers must check the return value; exact success/failure codes are not specified here.

A text string consisting of hexadecimal digits, optionally mixed case (0-9, a-f, A-F). It may include ignorable whitespace or separator characters when an ignore-set is provided to a decoder. It can represent binary data where each byte is encoded as two hex characters. NUL-termination is not required when an explicit length is supplied.

A text string containing Base64 data using a specified variant (e.g., standard, URL-safe, with/without padding). Valid characters include A–Z, a–z, 0–9, '+' and '/', or '-' and '_' for URL-safe, optionally '=' for padding, and may include ignorable whitespace when permitted. NUL-termination is not required when an explicit length is supplied.
